Prices and request fields on the API pages were checked against the live discovery documents on app.suedeai.ai; those documents (https://app.suedeai.ai/.well-known/x402 and https://app.suedeai.ai/api/v1/catalog) carry the current values.

## Suede Developer Docs | x402 APIs and Creator IP

URL: https://docs.suedeai.ai/
Last updated: 2026-11-15

> Read Suede developer docs for programmable IP, creator ownership, provenance, licensing, and x402 agent-commerce APIs. Browse the canonical GitHub source.

### Suede developer docs for programmable IP

Suede developer docs explain the public interfaces, rights concepts, and agent-commerce discovery surfaces in the Suede ecosystem. The canonical documentation is maintained in the [Suede-AI/suede-docs repository](https://github.com/Suede-AI/suede-docs) on GitHub.

#### API guides: pay-per-call endpoints

Suede sells music, video and image generation per call over x402, paid in USDC on Base with no account or API key. These guides cover the full integration, checked against the live API on 2026-10-11. For prices and request fields, the live discovery documents on `app.suedeai.ai` are the source of truth, and each guide links the documents it was checked against.

1. [Quickstart](https://docs.suedeai.ai/quickstart): send a request, read the 402 challenge, sign an EIP-3009 USDC authorization, retry with `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`, and poll for the result.
2. [Endpoints](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints): the three paid endpoints, their prices, shared payment terms, request headers and asynchronous mode.
3. [Create Music](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints/create-music): `POST /create-music`, a full original song from a prompt, $0.50.
4. [Agent Video](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints/agent-video): `POST /agent/video`, an 8-second 720p clip with native audio, $4.99.
5. [Agent Image](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints/agent-image): `POST /agent/image`, one PNG or JPEG, $0.15.
6. [Errors and limits](https://docs.suedeai.ai/errors): status codes, error bodies, rate limits, idempotency and versioning.
7. [Python SDK](https://docs.suedeai.ai/python-sdk): `pip install suede-ai`, a client that signs and retries the payment for you.
8. [Discovery and MCP](https://docs.suedeai.ai/discovery): the x402 manifest, OpenAPI spec, catalog, A2A agent card and MCP server.

#### What is Suede?

Suede is a company founded in 2024 by Jason Colapietro and based in West Palm Beach, Florida. Its official company website is [suedeai.ai](https://suedeai.ai), and its SEO and AEO practice is [Suede SEO](https://suedeai.agency/). These developer docs cover the company's creator products, programmable IP, provenance, rights metadata, licensing workflows, and agent-commerce interfaces, including x402 and ACP discovery surfaces.

#### What are Suede's core pillars?

- **Programmable IP:** interfaces for recording provenance, rights metadata, and machine-readable usage terms.
- **Creator ownership:** documentation for connecting creative work to creator-supplied identity and rights context.
- **Provenance:** source and metadata records that help people and software inspect where a media asset came from.
- **Licensing:** documented workflows for publishing terms and reviewing license activity.
- **Agent commerce:** public x402 and ACP discovery files that describe available services and current prices.

#### Who maintains the public docs?

Suede maintains this index and the canonical docs repository. For current leadership background, see [Jason Colapietro's public profile](https://suedeai.ai/founder).

#### Where do the full developer docs live?

The canonical, most current public documentation is maintained on GitHub at [Suede-AI/suede-docs](https://github.com/Suede-AI/suede-docs): full product directory, x402/ACP endpoint table, token references, and language guide. This page mirrors the core facts; the GitHub README is the source of truth.

[Read the full docs on GitHub](https://github.com/Suede-AI/suede-docs)

#### What does Suede expose for AI agents (x402/ACP)?

Suede publishes public x402 and ACP discovery surfaces for agent-callable media and rights services. Use the [live agent-commerce catalog](https://app.suedeai.ai/api/v1/catalog) for current availability and prices, and the [x402 discovery document](https://app.suedeai.ai/.well-known/x402) for machine-readable routes.

On 2026-10-11 the catalog held three endpoints, each paid per call in USDC on Base: [Create Music](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints/create-music) at $0.50, [Agent Video](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints/agent-video) at $4.99 and [Agent Image](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints/agent-image) at $0.15. The same offerings are published as an OpenAPI spec, an A2A agent card and an MCP server; the [discovery guide](https://docs.suedeai.ai/discovery) lists every format.

## x402 Quickstart: Pay a Suede API Call | Suede Docs

URL: https://docs.suedeai.ai/quickstart
Last updated: 2026-11-25

> Pay a Suede endpoint over x402: read the 402 challenge, sign an EIP-3009 USDC authorization on Base, retry with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE, then poll the job.

### Pay a Suede x402 endpoint in five steps

Suede sells music, video and image generation per call over x402. There is no account and no API key: your wallet signs a USDC payment on Base, and the same HTTP request carries it. This guide follows the flow the live endpoints at `app.suedeai.ai` run, checked on 2026-10-11.

#### What you need

- **USDC on Base mainnet** in a wallet you control. The lowest-priced call, [Agent Image](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints/agent-image), costs $0.15.
- **A way to sign EIP-712 typed data**, such as viem, ethers or eth-account. The [suede-ai Python SDK](https://docs.suedeai.ai/python-sdk) does the signing for you.
- **No ETH for gas.** Under the x402 `exact` scheme the facilitator submits the transfer and pays the gas. Your signature fixes the amount and the recipient, and the facilitator cannot change either.

#### 1. Read the price from the discovery document

Prices are enforced on the server, so read them before you sign. The x402 discovery document lists every paid resource:

```
curl -s https://app.suedeai.ai/.well-known/x402 \
  | jq -r '.resources[] | "\(.method) \(.resource) \(.priceUsd)"'
```

On 2026-10-11 it returned three resources:

```
POST https://app.suedeai.ai/create-music $0.50
POST https://app.suedeai.ai/agent/video $4.99
POST https://app.suedeai.ai/agent/image $0.15
```

The [discovery page](https://docs.suedeai.ai/discovery) covers the other machine-readable formats, including OpenAPI, the product catalog and the MCP server.

#### 2. Send the request and read the 402 challenge

Send the request you want to buy, with no payment attached:

```
curl -i -X POST https://app.suedeai.ai/agent/image \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"prompt":"Album cover, neon city at night, rain on glass","aspectRatio":"1:1","outputFormat":"png"}'
```

The server answers `402 Payment Required`. The challenge comes twice: as base64-encoded JSON in the `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` header, and as the same JSON in the body. Trimmed to the fields you sign against:

```
HTTP/2 402
content-type: application/json
payment-required: eyJ4NDAyVmVyc2lvbiI6IDIs...
suede-api-version: 1

{
  "x402Version": 2,
  "error": "PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header is required",
  "resource": { "url": "https://app.suedeai.ai/agent/image" },
  "accepts": [{
    "scheme": "exact",
    "network": "eip155:8453",
    "maxAmountRequired": "150000",
    "amount": "150000",
    "asset": "0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913",
    "payTo": "0x10FF767043A1723E0BB5B9207bC37D3442cC9E4F",
    "maxTimeoutSeconds": 300,
    "extra": { "name": "USD Coin", "version": "2", "decimals": 6, "priceUsd": "$0.15" }
  }]
}
```

| Field | What it tells you |
| --- | --- |
| `network` | `eip155:8453` is Base mainnet. |
| `asset` | The USDC contract on Base. It is also the EIP-712 `verifyingContract`. |
| `amount` | The price in USDC base units. USDC has 6 decimals, so `150000` is $0.15. |
| `payTo` | The address that receives the payment. |
| `maxTimeoutSeconds` | 300 seconds on all three endpoints. |
| `extra.name`, `extra.version` | The EIP-712 domain name and version: `"USD Coin"` and `"2"`. |

To read the header copy instead of the body, decode it:

```
curl -s -o /dev/null -D - -X POST https://app.suedeai.ai/agent/image \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"prompt":"test"}' \
  | grep -i '^payment-required:' | cut -d' ' -f2 | tr -d '\r' \
  | base64 -d | jq '.accepts[0]'
```

An unpaid request gets the 402 even when the body is empty, so the challenge does not mean your body is valid. Check it against the [endpoint reference](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints) before you sign.

#### 3. Sign an EIP-3009 authorization

USDC supports EIP-3009 `transferWithAuthorization`, so paying is a signature over EIP-712 typed data. You do not send a transaction yourself. Fill the typed data from the `accepts` entry:

```
domain
  name               "USD Coin"            accepts[0].extra.name
  version            "2"                   accepts[0].extra.version
  chainId            8453
  verifyingContract  0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913   accepts[0].asset

primaryType  TransferWithAuthorization
  from         address   your wallet
  to           address   0x10FF767043A1723E0BB5B9207bC37D3442cC9E4F   accepts[0].payTo
  value        uint256   150000                                       accepts[0].amount
  validAfter   uint256   a Unix time slightly in the past
  validBefore  uint256   a Unix time later than now + maxTimeoutSeconds
  nonce        bytes32   32 random bytes
```

For reference, the suede-ai SDK sets `validAfter` to 60 seconds before now and `validBefore` to now plus the larger of 600 seconds and `maxTimeoutSeconds` plus 60.

#### 4. Retry with the PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header

Wrap the signature in an x402 version 2 `PaymentPayload`. The `accepted` field repeats the `accepts` entry you chose:

```
{
  "x402Version": 2,
  "resource": { "url": "https://app.suedeai.ai/agent/image" },
  "accepted": {
    "scheme": "exact",
    "network": "eip155:8453",
    "amount": "150000",
    "asset": "0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913",
    "payTo": "0x10FF767043A1723E0BB5B9207bC37D3442cC9E4F",
    "maxTimeoutSeconds": 300,
    "extra": { "name": "USD Coin", "version": "2", "decimals": 6, "priceUsd": "$0.15" }
  },
  "payload": {
    "signature": "0x...",
    "authorization": {
      "from": "0xYourWallet",
      "to": "0x10FF767043A1723E0BB5B9207bC37D3442cC9E4F",
      "value": "150000",
      "validAfter": "1791746000",
      "validBefore": "1791746660",
      "nonce": "0x..."
    }
  }
}
```

Base64-encode that JSON and send the identical request again with it in `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`. Add an `X-Idempotency-Key`: if you resend the same key and body within the cache window, you get the original response back without a second charge.

```
curl -i -X POST https://app.suedeai.ai/agent/image \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "PAYMENT-SIGNATURE: $PAYMENT" \
  -H 'X-Idempotency-Key: cover-art-0001' \
  -d '{"prompt":"Album cover, neon city at night, rain on glass","aspectRatio":"1:1","outputFormat":"png"}'
```

A paid call answers `202 Accepted` with a job to poll. The discovery document gives this example body:

```
{
  "jobId": "image-job-example",
  "status": "queued",
  "provider": "suede",
  "pollUrl": "https://app.suedeai.ai/agent/image/image-job-example"
}
```

Paid calls are asynchronous by default because a render takes minutes and payment clients time out in about 30 seconds. To block until the asset is ready, add `?async=false` to the URL. Only the literal value `true` selects asynchronous mode: any other value, including `1`, `yes` and `on`, counts as `false` and blocks.

The same header also accepts a Skyfire `pay+jwt` or `kya-pay+jwt` token in place of an x402 payload.

#### 5. Poll for the result

Polling requires no new payment. Request the saved `pollUrl` until the job reaches a final state or your local deadline expires. A local timeout does not end the remote job; later, resume polling the same reference.

```
curl -s https://app.suedeai.ai/agent/image/<jobId>
```

| Endpoint | Poll route | Finished when | Asset field |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [/agent/image](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints/agent-image) | `GET /agent/image/{jobId}` | `status` is `completed` or `failed` | `imageUrl` |
| [/agent/video](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints/agent-video) | `GET /agent/video/{jobId}` | `status` is `completed` or `failed` | `videoUrl` |
| [/create-music](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints/create-music) | `GET /api/songs/{songId}` | `model_version` is no longer `pending` | `audio_url` |

For music, `audio_url` holds a placeholder cover image until the track is rendered, so check `model_version`, not `audio_url`. A value of `failed` is final. The [errors page](https://docs.suedeai.ai/errors) covers rate limits, retries and what is never charged.

#### Skip the signing code

The [suede-ai Python SDK](https://docs.suedeai.ai/python-sdk) runs steps 2 to 4 for you and returns the 202 body:

```
pip install suede-ai
```

```
from suede_ai import SuedeClient

with SuedeClient(wallet_private_key=PRIVATE_KEY) as suede:
    job = suede.agent_image(prompt="Album cover, neon city at night, rain on glass")
    print(job["pollUrl"])
```

#### Verify your integration before enabling payment

1. **Discovery:** fetch the [manifest and OpenAPI](https://docs.suedeai.ai/discovery) with no wallet configured. Match the exact method and URL; verify the expected fields and payment network.
2. **Challenge:** make the unsigned request in step 2. Check that the client presents the offered terms and stops before signing. For an agent, set a server-side amount cap and match the rail, resource, network, token and intended recipient before allowing payment.
3. **Job handling:** use local responses for 202, processing, completed and failed. Restart the worker after 202 and confirm it reads the same job instead of submitting a new one.
4. **Recovery:** simulate a timeout after submit and a throttled GET. The first should set aside the purchase for reconciliation; the second should only delay the next status read.

Only the submit step should be able to sign. Polling and downloading should run without wallet credentials. See the [recovery decisions](https://docs.suedeai.ai/errors#recovery-decisions) for what to retain when a request is interrupted.

#### Sell your own x402 endpoint

The same rail works in the other direction. [x402 Agent Builder: Get Paid Per Call](https://suedeai.app/x402-agent-builder): build an AI agent on a visual canvas, set a price per call, and get paid in USDC on Base through x402 once you enable payments. Dry runs need no wallet.

#### Frequently asked questions

##### What is x402?

x402 is a way to pay for an HTTP request inside the request itself. The server answers an unpaid request with `402 Payment Required` and the payment terms, and the client sends the same request again with a signed payment in the `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` header. Suede's endpoints use x402 version 2 with the `exact` scheme, settled in USDC on Base mainnet.

##### How much USDC do I need to make a first call?

The lowest-priced call, [Agent Image](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints/agent-image), costs $0.15. Fund the wallet with what you plan to spend and no more, because the key signs real USDC transfers. You need no ETH: the facilitator pays the gas.

##### Can I test the flow without spending anything?

Yes, up to the signature. Fetching the discovery documents and sending the unsigned request in step 2 cost nothing, and the 402 challenge shows the exact terms you would sign. Test job handling with local fixtures for `202`, processing, completed and failed responses before you enable payment.

##### Which libraries can sign the payment?

Any library that signs EIP-712 typed data, such as viem, ethers or eth-account. The [suede-ai Python SDK](https://docs.suedeai.ai/python-sdk) runs steps 2 to 4 for you and returns the 202 body.

##### What should my client do if the paid request times out?

Treat the outcome as unknown and do not sign a second payment for the same intent. Resend the same body with the same `X-Idempotency-Key` within the cache window to get the original response back without a second charge. The [errors page](https://docs.suedeai.ai/errors) lists what to keep for each kind of interruption.

#### Sources

Every value on this page comes from these documents, fetched on 2026-10-11, and from live requests to the endpoints on the same day.

- [app.suedeai.ai/openapi.json](https://app.suedeai.ai/openapi.json): asynchronous execution, the `async` parameter, idempotency and poll routes.
- [x402 HTTP transport, version 2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/coinbase/x402/main/specs/transports-v2/http.md): the `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` and `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` headers and the `PaymentPayload` shape.
- [x402 exact scheme on EVM](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/coinbase/x402/main/specs/schemes/exact/scheme_exact_evm.md): EIP-3009 signing and who pays gas.
- [EIP-3009](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3009): the `TransferWithAuthorization` type.
- [suede-ai 0.4.0 on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/suede-ai/): the SDK's signing window.

## Suede x402 API Endpoints and Prices | Suede Docs

URL: https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints
Last updated: 2026-11-25

> Three pay-per-call Suede endpoints for music, video and image generation, with prices, USDC amounts on Base, shared headers and poll routes.

### Suede x402 API endpoints

Three endpoints, one payment rail. Each is a `POST` to `https://app.suedeai.ai`, priced per call in USDC on Base, and a paid call returns a job you can poll for free. The figures below come from the live discovery document and OpenAPI spec. They were first checked on 2026-10-11, and the prices, payment terms, routes and response codes were checked again on 2026-11-25.

#### The three paid endpoints

| Endpoint | What you get | Price | amount | Poll route |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`POST /create-music`](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints/create-music) | A complete original song with vocals, melody and full arrangement, as a finished MP3 | $0.50 | `500000` | `GET /api/songs/{songId}` |
| [`POST /agent/video`](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints/agent-video) | An 8-second 720p clip with native audio | $4.99 | `4990000` | `GET /agent/video/{jobId}` |
| [`POST /agent/image`](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints/agent-image) | One hosted still image, PNG or JPEG | $0.15 | `150000` | `GET /agent/image/{jobId}` |

`amount` is the price in USDC base units (6 decimals), exactly as it appears in the 402 challenge and the value you sign. Each endpoint takes a JSON body in which `prompt` is the only required field.

#### Which endpoint fits the job

Pick by the asset you need to ship. The uses below are the ones each endpoint's live discovery entry names.

| You need | Call | What to put in the prompt |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A soundtrack under video, a podcast or game theme, a release-ready artist track or a demo sketch | [`POST /create-music`](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints/create-music) | Genre, mood, instrumentation and tempo. Supply your own lyrics, ask for an instrumental, or pin a style tag. |
| Short-form video, b-roll, a product shot, music-video visuals, a social clip or an ad | [`POST /agent/video`](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints/agent-video) | The scene and its sounds. Audio is generated from what the scene describes, so a silent scene renders near-silent. |
| Album or single cover art, a thumbnail, social or campaign graphics, concept art, a storyboard frame or an article illustration | [`POST /agent/image`](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints/agent-image) | The picture, plus an `aspectRatio` that matches the placement. |

A finished song from Create Music already comes with cover art in `image_url`. Call Agent Image when you need artwork in a specific framing, such as a `9:16` story or a `16:9` video thumbnail. Each call is its own purchase, so give each one its own `X-Idempotency-Key`.

#### The smallest valid request for each endpoint

Only `prompt` is required. These bodies are complete:

```
POST https://app.suedeai.ai/create-music
{"prompt": "Upbeat 80s synthwave with driving bass and neon atmosphere"}

POST https://app.suedeai.ai/agent/video
{"prompt": "Slow push-in on a spinning vinyl record, rain against the window, soft piano and the crackle of the needle"}

POST https://app.suedeai.ai/agent/image
{"prompt": "Album cover, neon city at night, rain on glass"}
```

The optional fields, with types and limits, are on each endpoint page:

- [Create Music](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints/create-music): `style`, `custom_mode`, `lyrics`, `make_instrumental`, `vocal_gender` and `tags`.
- [Agent Video](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints/agent-video): `durationSeconds` (default `8`, from `3` to `15`) and `aspectRatio` (`16:9`, `9:16` or `1:1`).
- [Agent Image](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints/agent-image): `aspectRatio` (ten ratios from `1:1` to `21:9`) and `outputFormat` (`png` or `jpeg`).

Send the body once without `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` to receive the 402 challenge. An unpaid request gets the 402 before the body is validated, so the challenge does not mean the body is valid. Check it against the endpoint page before you sign, because a paid call that fails validation comes back `422`.

#### Payment terms shared by all three

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `x402Version` | `2` |
| `scheme` | `exact` |
| `network` | `eip155:8453` (Base mainnet) |
| `asset` | `0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913` (USDC; EIP-712 domain `"USD Coin"`, version `"2"`) |
| `payTo` | `0x10FF767043A1723E0BB5B9207bC37D3442cC9E4F` |
| `maxTimeoutSeconds` | `300` |

The same `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` header also accepts Skyfire `pay+jwt` and `kya-pay+jwt` tokens. The product catalog lists Stripe Checkout as a second payment method at the same USD prices: 50, 499 and 15 cents. The [quickstart](https://docs.suedeai.ai/quickstart) walks through the x402 payment step by step.

#### Request headers

| Header | Required | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Content-Type: application/json` | Yes | All three endpoints take a JSON body. |
| `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` | For a paid call | A base64 x402 `PaymentPayload` or a Skyfire token. Leave it off the first call to receive the 402 challenge. |
| `X-Idempotency-Key` | No | Up to 200 characters. Resending the same key and body within the cache window returns the original response without charging again. |
| `Suede-API-Version` | No | Pins the API version. The current and only supported value is `1`. |

#### Asynchronous by default

A call that carries `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` queues the job and answers `202 Accepted` with a `pollUrl`. Renders take minutes, and x402 and Skyfire clients time out in about 30 seconds, so this keeps your payment client from timing out mid-render. Polling needs no further payment.

- `?async=false` forces a blocking call that answers `200` with the finished asset.
- `?async=true` queues the job. Only the literal `true` selects asynchronous mode; `1`, `yes` and `on` count as `false`.
- The body field `asyncMode` can switch asynchronous mode on, never off. `"asyncMode": false` leaves a paid call asynchronous.

All three endpoints answer `202` for a queued job, so a `2xx` other than `202` means the asset is already in the body.

#### Response codes

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `202` | Paid call accepted and queued. Poll `pollUrl`. |
| `200` | Blocking call finished, with the asset in the body. |
| `400` | Bad request, for example an unsupported `Suede-API-Version`. |
| `402` | Payment required, or the payment was not accepted. |
| `413` | Create Music only: the JSON body exceeds the 64 KiB ceiling, or a lower configured upload limit. |
| `422` | The body failed validation. A paid request that fails validation is not charged. |
| `429` | Rate-limited. Wait for `Retry-After`. |
| `5XX` | Server or upstream failure. Not charged; retry with the same `X-Idempotency-Key`. |

Bodies, headers and retry rules for each code are on the [errors page](https://docs.suedeai.ai/errors).

#### Collect the result: two poll shapes

Video and image polls follow the same `jobId` and `status` pattern. Music returns the song row instead, so a client that handles all three needs two parsers.

| Endpoint | Poll route | Finished when | Asset field | Unknown id |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `/create-music` | `GET /api/songs/{songId}` | `model_version` is no longer `pending` | `audio_url` | `404` |
| `/agent/video` | `GET /agent/video/{jobId}` | `status` is `completed` or `failed` | `videoUrl` | `200` with `status` `failed` |
| `/agent/image` | `GET /agent/image/{jobId}` | `status` is `completed` or `failed` | `imageUrl` | `200` with `status` `failed` |

For music, `audio_url` holds a placeholder cover image until the track is rendered, so read `model_version` first. A `model_version` of `failed` is final. Save the `pollUrl` from the 202 before you do anything else: a restarted worker should resume that poll, not buy the asset again.

#### Budget a batch of calls

Each call is priced on its own. Multiply the per-call price by the number of renders you plan to buy:

| Batch | Total | Total in base units |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 images | $1.50 | `1500000` |
| 10 songs | $5.00 | `5000000` |
| 10 video clips | $49.90 | `49900000` |

Polls, requests that fail validation (`422`), server failures (`5XX`) and a resend with the same `X-Idempotency-Key` and body within the cache window add nothing. A changed prompt or a deliberate second take is a new purchase. For an agent that spends on its own, set a server-side cap and compare each challenge's `amount` with it before signing, as the [quickstart](https://docs.suedeai.ai/quickstart) describes.

#### Frequently asked questions

##### Do I need a Suede account or an API key to call these endpoints?

No. The public x402 flow needs no Suede account and no API key. Your wallet signs a USDC payment on Base, and the same HTTP request carries it in the `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` header.

##### Do I need ETH on Base to pay for gas?

No. Under the x402 `exact` scheme the facilitator submits the USDC transfer and pays the gas. Your signature fixes the amount and the recipient.

##### Can I pay without signing a USDC transfer myself?

The `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` header also accepts Skyfire `pay+jwt` and `kya-pay+jwt` tokens. The product catalog lists Stripe Checkout as a second payment method at the same USD prices. The [Python SDK](https://docs.suedeai.ai/python-sdk) signs the x402 payment for you if you would rather not write signing code.

##### Why did my paid call return 202 instead of the file?

Paid calls are asynchronous by default. A render takes minutes and payment clients time out in about 30 seconds, so the call queues the job and returns a `pollUrl`. Poll it for free, or add `?async=false` to block until the asset is ready.

##### Am I charged when a request fails?

Not for a `422` validation failure, a `5XX` server failure, any poll, or a resend with the same idempotency key and body within the cache window. Retry a `5XX` with the same `X-Idempotency-Key`.

##### Are the older /v1 routes still available?

They are not in the live x402 manifest. The Python SDK still ships helpers for some older `/v1/*` routes, but new integrations should target the three endpoints on this page.

##### Where do I check the current price before I sign?

Read [app.suedeai.ai/.well-known/x402](https://app.suedeai.ai/.well-known/x402). Prices are enforced on the server, and the `amount` in the 402 challenge is the value to sign.

#### Sources

- [app.suedeai.ai/.well-known/x402](https://app.suedeai.ai/.well-known/x402): resources, prices and payment requirements.
- [app.suedeai.ai/openapi.json](https://app.suedeai.ai/openapi.json): headers, the `async` parameter and response codes.
- [app.suedeai.ai/api/v1/catalog](https://app.suedeai.ai/api/v1/catalog): product descriptions and payment methods.

For every machine-readable format these endpoints are published in, see [discovery documents and MCP server](https://docs.suedeai.ai/discovery).

## Create Music API: POST /create-music | Suede Docs

URL: https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints/create-music
Last updated: 2026-10-11

> POST /create-music turns a text prompt into a full original song for $0.50 USDC on Base. Request fields, the 202 job response and how to poll it.

### Create Music: POST /create-music

Turn a text prompt into a complete original song, with vocals, melody and full arrangement, delivered as a finished MP3 rather than a loop or preview. One call costs $0.50 in USDC on Base.

#### What it is for

Describe the genre, mood, instrumentation and tempo, supply your own lyrics, ask for an instrumental, or pin a style tag. The discovery document names soundtracks under video, release-ready artist tracks, podcast and game themes, and demo sketches as uses.

#### At a glance

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Endpoint | `POST https://app.suedeai.ai/create-music` |
| Price | $0.50, `amount` `500000` USDC base units |
| Payment | x402 `exact` on `eip155:8453` to `0x10FF767043A1723E0BB5B9207bC37D3442cC9E4F`, or a Skyfire token |
| Paid response | `202 Accepted` with a job envelope; save `pollUrl` when returned |
| Poll | `GET https://app.suedeai.ai/api/songs/{songId}`, free |
| Identifiers | OpenAPI `operationId`, A2A skill and MCP tool: `create_music` |

#### Request body

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `prompt` | string | Yes | The song you want: genre, mood, instruments and any specific vibe. Examples from the schema: "Upbeat 80s synthwave with driving bass and neon atmosphere", "A melancholic acoustic guitar ballad about rain". |
| `style` | string | No | A style or genre tag, such as `Hip Hop`, `Ambient` or `Rock`. |
| `custom_mode` | boolean | No | `true` to sing the lyrics you supply in `lyrics`. |
| `lyrics` | string | When `custom_mode` is `true` | Your lyrics. |
| `make_instrumental` | boolean | No | `true` for a track without vocals. |
| `vocal_gender` | string | No | `m` or `f`. |
| `tags` | string | No | Comma-separated keywords to tag the generated file. |
| `asyncMode` | boolean | No | Switches asynchronous mode on, never off. Paid calls are already asynchronous. |

#### Example: your own lyrics

First send the request without `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` to get the 402 challenge (`amount` `500000`, `priceUsd` `$0.50`), sign it as shown in the [quickstart](https://docs.suedeai.ai/quickstart), then send:

```
curl -i -X POST https://app.suedeai.ai/create-music \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "PAYMENT-SIGNATURE: $PAYMENT" \
  -H 'X-Idempotency-Key: rain-ballad-0001' \
  -d '{
    "prompt": "A melancholic acoustic guitar ballad about rain",
    "style": "Ambient",
    "custom_mode": true,
    "lyrics": "Your lyrics here",
    "vocal_gender": "f"
  }'
```

For a track without vocals, drop `custom_mode` and `lyrics` and send `"make_instrumental": true`.

#### Response to a paid call: 202 Accepted

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `status` | `processing` or `queued`. |
| `shareUrl` | The browser share URL the track will have once the job completes. |
| `songId` | The id of the song row, and the `{songId}` in `pollUrl`. It can be `null` when the job is queued before that row exists. |
| `pollUrl` | The absolute URL of `GET /api/songs/{songId}`. No further payment. |

With `?async=false` the call blocks and answers `200` with `shareUrl` (a public page to listen to and download the track), `title` and `imageUrl` (cover art). Renders take minutes and payment clients time out in about 30 seconds, so the default asynchronous mode suits most callers.

#### Polling: GET /api/songs/{songId}

Music returns the song row, not the `jobId` and `status` shape the video and image polls use. Read `model_version`:

- `pending`: the track is queued or rendering. Poll again.
- `failed`: generation failed. This is final; stop polling.
- Any version label, such as `v4.5`: the track is ready and `audio_url` is the finished MP3.

Until the track is ready, `audio_url` holds the placeholder cover-image URL the row was created with. It is a reachable image, not audio, so a present `audio_url` does not mean the track is finished.

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | The `songId` you polled. |
| `model_version` | The job state, as above. |
| `audio_url` | The finished MP3 once ready; a placeholder image URL before that. |
| `title`, `prompt`, `genre` | Track title, the prompt it was generated from, and the style label from the request. |
| `image_url` | Cover art URL. |
| `duration` | Length in seconds; `0` until the render finishes. |
| `share_id` | Public share identifier for the listener page. |
| `is_public` | `true` for x402 and Skyfire paid jobs, which are created public so the buyer can fetch them. |
| `created_at` | Creation time, ISO 8601. |

An unknown `songId` answers `404` with `{"error":"Song not found"}`. A 404 means no accessible song row was found for that lookup, not that the track is still rendering.

#### Choose the right request mode

For generated vocals, describe the song rather than supplying a lyrics field. Start with genre, mood, instrumentation and structure. For a podcast opener, for example, ask for a restrained intro, a recognizable motif, and space for speech. Treat tempo, structure and length in the brief as creative direction, not timing guarantees; cut the delivered audio to picture after review.

For supplied lyrics, use `custom_mode: true` and put the intended words in `lyrics`. Keep arrangement instructions in `prompt`. Use text you are authorized to transmit, and do not send confidential lyrics or client information: paid tracks are created public and the song record can include the prompt.

For an instrumental, omit `custom_mode`, `lyrics` and `vocal_gender`. Use one clear direction rather than mixing instrumental and vocal instructions:

```
{
  "prompt": "Quiet documentary underscore. Felt piano, soft strings, no percussion, sparse texture under spoken narration.",
  "style": "Ambient",
  "make_instrumental": true
}
```

For original generated vocals:

```
{
  "prompt": "Mid-tempo indie folk song with a close vocal, brushed drums and acoustic guitar; restrained verses and a wider final chorus.",
  "style": "Indie Folk"
}
```

Use the published request schema for automation. The SDK can send other values in its convenience methods; an argument being transmitted does not mean the server guarantees an exact duration, file size, or arrangement.

#### From payment approval to delivery

1. Give each intended purchase its own `X-Idempotency-Key` and retain the original JSON. A changed prompt or intentional new take is a new purchase, not a retry.
2. Read the current terms from the [discovery document](https://docs.suedeai.ai/discovery) and verify the payment challenge before signing. Check network, asset, recipient, amount and resource against your budget and allowlist. Keep the signing key and `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` out of URLs, logs and browser code.
3. Use the default asynchronous mode. Save the response, its `pollUrl` if present, its `songId` when available, and the locally recorded payment reference. A `202` confirms acceptance, not audio delivery. Save a valid `pollUrl` even when `songId` is absent; never construct a URL ending in `null`.
4. Poll without payment. Read `model_version` first. `pending` means wait even if `audio_url` returns HTTP 200. `failed` is terminal. A nonempty version label and a valid media URL give you a candidate for delivery.
5. Download the candidate as media, not the `shareUrl` listener page or the `image_url` cover. Check successful HTTP status, audio content type and playable, decodable bytes before marking a job delivered. Store the version, duration and your verified output reference in your own records.

If you already received a job reference, resume the existing poll after a restart. If a signed POST timed out and no response was saved, reconcile the payment reference before sending a newly signed purchase. Treat a submit timeout as an unknown job outcome. Use the original key for a permitted replay within the cache window; reconcile payment separately.

#### Bounded polling in Python

This `httpx` example takes the saved `pollUrl` from an accepted request. It performs no paid calls and does not download the file. The three-minute deadline is a client choice, not a service limit. Timeout means the polling worker stopped, not that it canceled the generation.

```
import time
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

import httpx

def wait_for_song(poll_url: str, max_wait: float = 180) -> str:
    url = urlsplit(poll_url)
    path = url.path.split("/")
    if (url.scheme != "https" or url.netloc != "app.suedeai.ai"
            or len(path) != 4 or path[:3] != ["", "api", "songs"]
            or path[3] in ("", ".", "..") or url.query or url.fragment):
        raise ValueError("Unexpected song polling URL")

    deadline = time.monotonic() + max_wait
    delay = 3.0
    with httpx.Client(follow_redirects=False) as client:
        while (remaining := deadline - time.monotonic()) > 0:
            pause = delay
            try:
                response = client.get(
                    poll_url, timeout=min(10.0, remaining)
                )
            except httpx.TransportError:
                pass  # transient network error; retry only the free GET
            else:
                if response.status_code == 404:
                    raise LookupError("Song not found; check the saved reference")
                if response.status_code in (429, 502, 503, 504):
                    retry_after = response.headers.get("Retry-After", "")
                    if retry_after.isascii() and retry_after.isdecimal():
                        pause = max(pause, int(retry_after))
                else:
                    response.raise_for_status()
                    song = response.json()
                    version = song.get("model_version")
                    if version == "failed":
                        raise RuntimeError("Music generation failed")
                    if version != "pending":
                        audio_url = song.get("audio_url")
                        if isinstance(version, str) and version.strip() and isinstance(audio_url, str):
                            audio = urlsplit(audio_url)
                            if audio.scheme == "https" and audio.hostname:
                                return audio_url
                        raise ValueError("Song result is missing version or audio URL")
            time.sleep(max(0, min(pause, deadline - time.monotonic())))
            delay = min(delay * 1.5, 15.0)

    raise TimeoutError("Still unresolved; save the poll URL and resume later")
```

Before using the returned URL in a server-side downloader, apply your media-host allowlist and check any redirect destination independently. An HTTPS URL alone does not prove that it serves MP3 audio.

#### Test the states without paying

Use local fixtures with placeholder values. These examples illustrate fields the poller should act on, not complete API responses or URLs to fetch.

```
{"id":"example-song","model_version":"pending","audio_url":"https://example.invalid/cover.png"}
{"id":"example-song","model_version":"failed","audio_url":null}
{"id":"example-song","model_version":"v4.5","audio_url":"https://example.invalid/track.mp3"}
```

- In the first case assert that no download starts, even if the cover URL says `200`.
- In the second case assert that the poller stops and does not resubmit.
- In the third case assert that the downloader receives the media URL, not the public share page. Simulate a response with `image/png` or HTML and require a delivery error.
- Also test `429` with a numeric `Retry-After`, a transport timeout, a `404`, and a worker restart using an existing poll URL. Do not attach credentials to any poll request.

#### Troubleshooting and retry decisions

| What you see | Next action |
| --- | --- |
| First POST returns `402` | Read the challenge. Authorize only after verifying the current terms. A repeated `402` is a signal to inspect the challenge or payment result, not to sign in a loop. |
| `400`, `413` or `422` on POST | Check the API version, body size and field errors. Fix the request before another authorization; do not retry the same malformed body. |
| Poll returns `429` | Honor `Retry-After`, back off and resume the same GET. Avoid one polling loop per UI tab. |
| Poll returns `404` | Check the original reference and whether the app used the right route. Not the pending signal; do not pay again based on this alone. |
| Accepted, but client deadline passes | Persist the original handle and resume later. Distinguish local timeout from a server-side `failed` status. |
| Version label present but audio does not play | Verify the media response and bytes instead of relying on extension or status alone. Retain the song ID and report a delivery issue without a new purchase. |

For transport and payment recovery rules see [Errors, rate limits and retries](https://docs.suedeai.ai/errors). For signing and budget checks see the [x402 quickstart](https://docs.suedeai.ai/quickstart).

#### Sources

- [app.suedeai.ai/.well-known/x402](https://app.suedeai.ai/.well-known/x402): description, price, payment requirement and input schema (resource entry last updated 2026-08-30).
- [app.suedeai.ai/openapi.json](https://app.suedeai.ai/openapi.json): operations `create_music` and `create_music_result`.
- Live requests on 2026-10-11: the unpaid 402 challenge and the 404 for an unknown `songId`.

## Agent Video API: POST /agent/video | Suede Docs

URL: https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints/agent-video
Last updated: 2026-10-11

> Generate a short video with native audio for $4.99 USDC on Base. Plan the shot, authorize one render, poll the job, verify the MP4 and prepare it for release.

### Agent Video: POST /agent/video

Turn a written shot into a short video with native audio. Budget $4.99 USDC on Base per render, then retrieve the result without another payment. The default target is eight seconds at 720p; inspect the actual clip before using it in an edit.

#### What it is for

Short-form video, b-roll, product shots, music-video visuals, social clips and ads. The audio is generated from the scene, so write the sound into the prompt: instruments, voices, weather, movement. A silent scene renders near-silent by design.

#### At a glance

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Endpoint | `POST https://app.suedeai.ai/agent/video` |
| Price | $4.99, `amount` `4990000` USDC base units |
| Payment | x402 `exact` on `eip155:8453` to `0x10FF767043A1723E0BB5B9207bC37D3442cC9E4F`, or a Skyfire token |
| Output | A short clip with native audio; default target: 8 seconds at 720p |
| Paid response | `202 Accepted` with `jobId` and `pollUrl` |
| Poll | `GET https://app.suedeai.ai/agent/video/{jobId}`, free |
| Identifiers | OpenAPI `operationId`, A2A skill and MCP tool: `agent_video` |

#### Request body

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `prompt` | string | Yes | Narrative or visual prompt that drives the video concept. |
| `durationSeconds` | integer | No | Requested length in seconds. Default `8`, minimum `3`, maximum `15`. The service maps it to a supported render length. |
| `aspectRatio` | string | No | `16:9` (landscape, default), `9:16` (portrait) or `1:1` (square). |
| `asyncMode` | boolean | No | Default `false`. Switches asynchronous mode on, never off. Paid calls are already asynchronous. |

#### Choose the frame before writing the prompt

Start with the editor’s cut, not adjectives. Write one sentence for each of four things: what the viewer sees first, what changes, where the camera ends, and what the viewer hears when the action happens. If the sentence needs “meanwhile” or “cut to,” split it into shots. Each separately generated shot is another paid render.

A landscape banner can use horizontal movement and empty space for a headline. Portrait clips have less room beside the subject, so use depth or vertical movement instead. For square placements, center the decisive action and test a square preview. An aspect-ratio request describes the intended frame, not a guarantee that every subject or overlay will fit.

##### Landscape: show how a pour-over starts

```
{
  "prompt": "Single locked wide shot across a cafe counter. A glass brewer sits on the right; leave the left third empty for a title. A hand tilts a kettle above the brewer, a thin stream touches the grounds, then the first drop lands in the glass. Quiet room tone, soft pouring, one clear drip. No speech or music.",
  "aspectRatio": "16:9",
  "durationSeconds": 8
}
```

Acceptance check: pause on the first drop. Are both the pour and its destination visible? Can an editor add a headline on the left without covering either? If a headline must be spelled exactly, add it in the editor rather than asking the model to paint the words into the scene.

#### Example: a vertical social clip

Get the 402 challenge first (`amount` `4990000`, `priceUsd` `$4.99`), sign it as shown in the [quickstart](https://docs.suedeai.ai/quickstart), then send:

```
curl -i -X POST https://app.suedeai.ai/agent/video \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "PAYMENT-SIGNATURE: $PAYMENT" \
  -H 'X-Idempotency-Key: vinyl-clip-0001' \
  -d '{
    "prompt": "Slow push-in on a spinning vinyl record, rain against the window, soft piano and the crackle of the needle",
    "aspectRatio": "9:16"
  }'
```

The prompt names its sounds (rain, piano, needle crackle) because the audio track is generated from what the scene describes.

#### Response to a paid call: 202 Accepted

The discovery document gives this example body:

```
{
  "jobId": "video-job-example",
  "status": "queued",
  "provider": "suede",
  "pollUrl": "https://app.suedeai.ai/agent/video/video-job-example"
}
```

With `?async=false` the call blocks and answers `200` with the same body shape as the poll below, so one parser covers both paths. Renders take minutes and payment clients time out in about 30 seconds, so most callers should keep the default and poll.

#### Polling: GET /agent/video/{jobId}

Poll until `status` is `completed`, with `videoUrl` set, or `failed`. Both are final; `queued` and `processing` mean poll again.

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `jobId` | The render's job identifier. |
| `status` | `queued`, `processing`, `completed` or `failed`. |
| `provider` | The provider handling the render. |
| `videoUrl` | The generated video once complete; `null` until then. |
| `videoId` | The Suede video record identifier, when available. |
| `pageUrl` | The Suede share page, when available. |
| `pollUrl` | Set on the 202 accept; `null` on a poll response. |

An unknown or expired `jobId` answers `200` with `status` `failed`, not 404. On 2026-10-11 that response also carried `"error": "Generation failed. Please try again."` and an `etaSeconds` field set to `null`.

#### Plan and review a single-shot product clip

A shot list for a full commercial is a poor brief for one short render. For a record shop teaser, choose one visible action and one sound cue: “Vertical close-up of a turntable in a quiet shop. A hand lowers the needle. Hold on the spinning label as a soft vinyl crackle begins.” That gives the editor something concrete to accept or reject.

1. **Before the call:** choose the intended placement and aspect ratio. Decide whether the clip must loop, carry a caption or leave room for a price overlay. For a loop, brief continuous motion instead of a one-time action like the needle drop.
2. **While it renders:** save the job ID and poll URL from the accepted response. A queued job is not a finished clip. Use its status URL to check progress rather than submitting the scene again.
3. **At review:** watch once muted to judge framing and motion. Then listen without captions. Does the crackle begin with the needle, and is there room for the planned voiceover? Scrub the first and last frames if the placement requires a loop.

If the shot works but the caption covers the label, reposition the caption in the edit. If the needle never enters frame, rewrite that action as the subject of the shot before authorizing another render. Save the chosen clip and note which check failed on any rejected take.

#### Keep one authorization attached to one shot

1. Save the exact request body. Create a fresh idempotency key for this shot and keep it with the body. The example key above is illustrative, not a key to share across customers or projects.
2. Send the same JSON without a payment signature to receive the challenge. Compare its amount, token, network and recipient to the approved spend. Stop if any differ. A challenge is not a render.
3. Use your payment client to authorize, then submit the same body with the key. Keep payment credentials out of logs. Save the accepted job ID and poll URL before doing other work. Only the creation request needs the payment header; never forward it when retrieving the media.
4. If the connection drops after sending, first recover the saved job or original response. If a replay is necessary, use the same key and identical body within the service’s idempotency cache window. A fresh key, changed prompt or later replay is not a safe way to recover an existing charge.

The four JSON fields in the request table are the public controls. There is no published request field for a custom resolution, frame rate, fixed seed, subtitle file or separate soundtrack. A requested length of 15 seconds is valid input, not a promise of 15 seconds of footage. Plan a longer sequence as independently reviewed shots or extend it in an editor.

#### Collect the result without resubmitting the shot

Here is a Python 3 collector for a previously accepted job. Pass the saved absolute `pollUrl` as its only argument. It makes only free GET requests, waits between checks, honors numeric retry delays, and stops after at most 20 requests. A local stop is not a cancellation. Save the job and resume later instead of paying again.

```
import json, sys, time
from urllib.error import HTTPError, URLError
from urllib.parse import urlsplit
from urllib.request import urlopen

url = sys.argv[1]
u = urlsplit(url)
if (u.scheme, u.netloc) != ("https", "app.suedeai.ai") or not u.path.startswith("/agent/video/"):
    sys.exit("Expected the Suede video poll URL from the 202 response.")
for attempt in range(20):
    delay = min(5 * (attempt + 1), 30)
    try:
        with urlopen(url, timeout=15) as r:
            job = json.load(r)
    except HTTPError as e:
        if e.code != 429 and not 500 <= e.code <= 599:
            sys.exit(f"Poll HTTP {e.code}; inspect saved job. No new render.")
        hint = e.headers.get("Retry-After")
        if hint and (not hint.isdecimal() or int(hint) > 60):
            sys.exit(f"Resume after Retry-After: {hint}")
        delay = max(delay, int(hint or 0))
    except (URLError, TimeoutError):
        pass  # Retry only this GET.
    else:
        state = job.get("status")
        if state == "completed" and job.get("videoUrl"):
            print(job["videoUrl"])
            break
        if state not in ("queued", "processing"):
            sys.exit(f"Inspect job: {state!r}; no usable asset or job failed.")
    if attempt < 19:
        time.sleep(delay)
else:
    sys.exit("Polling paused. Keep the job ID and resume later.")
```

A 200 response only means the status lookup succeeded. A failed job, an unexpected state, malformed JSON or a completed job without media all require inspection, not another paid POST. Keep the last response and the job ID for troubleshooting. For a validation error on creation, check the exact field named in the response before making a corrected request.

#### Download the MP4, not the share page

Use `videoUrl` for the media itself. `pageUrl`, when present, is for a human to open in a browser. Saving that page as `.mp4` gives an editor HTML rather than footage. Do not reconstruct either link from `jobId` or `videoId`.

Set `VIDEO_URL` to the completed job’s media URL. This example follows HTTPS redirects, records the final content type and saves a candidate download. Verify it before assigning an MP4 extension.

```
curl --fail --show-error --silent --location --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' \
  --max-time 120 --output take.download --write-out '%{content_type}\n' "$VIDEO_URL"
ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=format_name,duration:stream=codec_type,width,height \
  -of json take.download
```

Expect MP4 media (normally `video/mp4`), a decodable video stream and a plausible duration. If the server reports `application/octet-stream`, inspect the container rather than assuming it is broken. If it returns HTML, an error or a zero-byte file, stop. Compare frame dimensions with the placement and check for an audio stream if sound is part of the brief. Rename the verified file and store it with the prompt, job ID and review decision.

#### Review the deliverable, not just the render status

- **First and last frames:** compare the opening with your thumbnail and the ending with the next shot. If a usable opening or hold exists, trim the clip instead of commissioning another one.
- **Movement and continuity:** watch at normal speed, then scrub through hands, reflections, object edges and contact points. A pleasing still does not establish that the motion works.
- **Sound and captions:** play the final edit muted. Is the point still clear? Caption speech and meaningful sound cues such as “[needle crackles]”; review timing and wording manually. If a visual action is essential but not explained aloud, supply a descriptive transcript or audio description appropriate to the placement.
- **Placement:** preview in the actual player at phone size. Check that captions, controls and platform overlays do not cover the subject. Check for distracting flashes and sudden audio jumps. Do not publish automatically just because the job completed.

Keep a short review record: “Pass: first drip visible and audible. Edit: add captions. Hold: mobile title overlaps kettle.” A failed technical download calls for another retrieval of the existing media; a new creative take calls for a changed brief and a new spending decision.

#### Sources

- [app.suedeai.ai/.well-known/x402](https://app.suedeai.ai/.well-known/x402): description, price, payment requirement, input schema and example output (resource entry last updated 2026-08-30).
- [app.suedeai.ai/openapi.json](https://app.suedeai.ai/openapi.json): operations `agent_video` and `agent_video_status`.
- Live requests on 2026-10-11: the unpaid 402 challenge and a poll for an unknown `jobId`.

## Agent Image API: POST /agent/image | Suede Docs

URL: https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints/agent-image
Last updated: 2026-10-11

> POST /agent/image returns one PNG or JPEG for $0.15 USDC on Base. Request fields, the ten aspect ratios, the 202 job response and the poll route.

### Agent Image: POST /agent/image

Generate one hosted still image from a text prompt, as PNG or JPEG. One call costs $0.15 in USDC on Base, the lowest price of the three endpoints, which also makes it the cheapest way to test a full payment round trip.

#### What it is for

Album and single cover art, podcast and video thumbnails, social and campaign graphics, concept art, storyboard frames, product shots and article illustrations. Frame it square, portrait or widescreen.

#### At a glance

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Endpoint | `POST https://app.suedeai.ai/agent/image` |
| Price | $0.15, `amount` `150000` USDC base units |
| Payment | x402 `exact` on `eip155:8453` to `0x10FF767043A1723E0BB5B9207bC37D3442cC9E4F`, or a Skyfire token |
| Output | One hosted PNG or JPEG |
| Paid response | `202 Accepted` with `jobId` and `pollUrl` |
| Poll | `GET https://app.suedeai.ai/agent/image/{jobId}`, free |
| Identifiers | OpenAPI `operationId`, A2A skill and MCP tool: `agent_image` |

#### Make your first call without spending

First confirm your client can reach the endpoint and read a payment challenge. The following request has no payment credential. It requests a challenge, not a render.

```
curl -sS -i https://app.suedeai.ai/agent/image \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Suede-API-Version: 1' \
  --data-binary '{"prompt":"An unlettered red record sleeve on a cream counter","aspectRatio":"1:1","outputFormat":"png"}'
```

1. Expect HTTP `402`. Inspect `x402Version`, `resource.url` and `accepts`. A challenge is not a successful request and does not prove the image body is valid.
2. Compare the resource and accepted payment terms with the [live discovery manifest](https://app.suedeai.ai/.well-known/x402) and your own allowlist. For direct x402, check the network, token, recipient and amount before signing. The price shown in this guide is a reference, not approval to spend.
3. When authorized to spend, use the [x402 quickstart](https://docs.suedeai.ai/quickstart) or [Python SDK](https://docs.suedeai.ai/python-sdk) to submit the same URL and body with `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`. Save the returned job before showing the caller a success screen.

The public x402 flow does not require a Suede account or Suede API key. The published OpenAPI also documents a Skyfire pay or kya-pay JWT supplied in the same header for the Skyfire rail. Treat both as sensitive. Keep wallet keys, signatures and payment tokens out of browser code, logs and analytics. A GET of the returned job URL does not require another authorization.

#### Request body

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `prompt` | string | Yes | Visual prompt describing the image to generate. |
| `aspectRatio` | string | No | One of `1:1`, `9:16`, `16:9`, `3:4`, `4:3`, `3:2`, `2:3`, `5:4`, `4:5`, `21:9`. |
| `outputFormat` | string | No | `png` or `jpeg`. |
| `asyncMode` | boolean | No | Switches asynchronous mode on, never off. Paid calls are already asynchronous. |

The ten aspect ratios cover square (`1:1`), portrait (`4:5`, `3:4`, `2:3`, `9:16`) and landscape or widescreen (`5:4`, `4:3`, `3:2`, `16:9`, `21:9`) framing.

#### Choose an execution mode before you sign

| Request | Mode | What the client should do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Paid POST without an `async` query parameter | Async, even with `asyncMode: false` | Handle `202`; store the job ID and status URL. |
| `?async=true` | Async; wins over the body | Use this literal if explicitly choosing async. |
| `?async=false` | Blocking; wins over the body | Inspect the body even on `200`. It can report processing or failure without an image. |

Use the default for paid calls unless you have a reason to block. Do not send `?async=1`, `yes` or `on`; the implementation treats them as false. There is no documented caller-controlled pixel-size, seed, transparency, or edit input in the request. Check the file you receive rather than inferring its properties from the prompt.

#### Example: square cover art

Get the 402 challenge first (`amount` `150000`, `priceUsd` `$0.15`), sign it as shown in the [quickstart](https://docs.suedeai.ai/quickstart), then send:

```
curl -i -X POST https://app.suedeai.ai/agent/image \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "PAYMENT-SIGNATURE: $PAYMENT" \
  -H 'X-Idempotency-Key: cover-art-0001' \
  -d '{
    "prompt": "Album cover, neon city at night, rain on glass",
    "aspectRatio": "1:1",
    "outputFormat": "png"
  }'
```

#### Response to a paid call: 202 Accepted

The discovery document gives this example body:

```
{
  "jobId": "image-job-example",
  "status": "queued",
  "provider": "suede",
  "pollUrl": "https://app.suedeai.ai/agent/image/image-job-example"
}
```

With `?async=false`, a successful HTTP response is `200` with the same response fields as the poll below. Read `status` before treating it as a finished asset.

#### Polling: GET /agent/image/{jobId}

Poll until `status` is `completed`, with `imageUrl` set, or `failed`. Both are final; `queued` and `processing` mean poll again.

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `jobId` | The render's job identifier. |
| `status` | `queued`, `processing`, `completed` or `failed`. |
| `provider` | The provider handling the render. |
| `imageUrl` | The generated image once complete; `null` until then. |
| `pollUrl` | Set on the 202 accept; `null` on a poll response. |

An unknown or expired `jobId` answers `200` with `status` `failed`, not 404. On 2026-10-11 that response looked like this:

```
{"jobId":"unknown-job-id","imageUrl":null,"status":"failed","provider":"suede","pollUrl":null,"error":"Generation failed. Please try again."}
```

#### One campaign, two placements: crop or generate again?

Suppose a record shop needs a square release tile and a vertical story. If the customer expects the same photograph in both placements, start with one image. Ask for the record sleeve in the center, with enough background around it for a crop. A second prompt is a new generation, not a resize of the first image.

1. **Brief the composition.** For a square tile, try: “Overhead photograph of a red record sleeve on a cream counter, sleeve centered, blank space above, no lettering.” Add the shop name in your layout after the image is ready so its spelling and placement stay under your control.
2. **Test both crops before buying another render.** Place the returned file in the square tile and a 9:16 story mockup. Check whether either crop cuts off the sleeve, hides the title area or leaves a price sticker unreadable at phone size.
3. **Make the revision match the problem.** If only the lettering fails, fix the overlay. If the vertical crop removes the subject, request a separate 9:16 composition. Review the current challenge before approving that additional paid call.

For handoff, keep the accepted image, its placement, the request body and the job ID together. Record whether the story is a crop or a separate render. That gives the next designer a specific asset to revise rather than a prompt to guess from.

#### Poll an accepted job with Python

Pass the `pollUrl` saved from your `202` response. This standard-library example uses only GET and never authorizes another payment. It backs off on throttling, server errors and transport errors, and stops on a failed job or a payment reconciliation signal. It schedules requests within an overall polling window and gives each request its own socket timeout. A production worker can schedule individual polls instead of sleeping.

```
import json
import time
from urllib.error import HTTPError, URLError
from urllib.parse import urlsplit
from urllib.request import HTTPRedirectHandler, Request, build_opener

class NoRedirect(HTTPRedirectHandler):
    def redirect_request(self, req, fp, code, msg, headers, newurl):
        return None

def poll_image(poll_url, *, deadline_seconds=120, request_timeout=10):
    url = urlsplit(poll_url)
    if (url.scheme, url.netloc) != ("https", "app.suedeai.ai"):
        raise ValueError("Use the status URL returned by Suede")
    if not url.path.startswith("/agent/image/") or url.query or url.fragment:
        raise ValueError("Expected an Agent Image status URL")

    opener = build_opener(NoRedirect())
    deadline = time.monotonic() + deadline_seconds
    delay = 1.0
    while (remaining := deadline - time.monotonic()) > 0:
        pause = delay
        try:
            req = Request(poll_url, headers={"Accept": "application/json"})
            with opener.open(req, timeout=min(request_timeout, remaining)) as res:
                raw = res.read(65537)
                if len(raw) > 65536:
                    raise RuntimeError("Status response too large")
                job = json.loads(raw)
        except HTTPError as exc:
            if exc.code == 402:
                raise RuntimeError("Reconcile the original payment") from exc
            if exc.code != 429 and not 500 <= exc.code <= 599:
                raise
            retry_after = exc.headers.get("Retry-After", "")
            if retry_after:
                if not (retry_after.isascii() and retry_after.isdecimal()):
                    raise TimeoutError("Defer polling using Retry-After") from exc
                seconds = retry_after.lstrip("0") or "0"
                if len(seconds) > 2 or int(seconds) > 30:
                    raise TimeoutError("Defer polling using Retry-After") from exc
                pause = max(pause, int(seconds))
        except (URLError, TimeoutError):
            pass
        else:
            status = job["status"]
            if status == "completed":
                result = job.get("imageUrl")
                if not isinstance(result, str) or not result:
                    raise RuntimeError("Completed without an image URL")
                return result
            if status == "failed":
                raise RuntimeError(job.get("error") or "Render failed")
            if status not in ("queued", "processing"):
                raise RuntimeError(f"Unexpected job status: {status}")
        time.sleep(max(0, min(pause, deadline - time.monotonic())))
        delay = min(delay * 2, 10.0)
    raise TimeoutError("Polling deadline reached; resume the same job later")
```

The return value is an image URL, not downloaded bytes. Pass it to the [asset delivery](#delivery) step. Keep the saved job if this function times out. Its backoff is capped at 10 seconds, and it honors numeric server hints of up to 30 seconds. If your deployment uses longer retry hints or HTTP-date hints, defer the job to your scheduler instead of polling sooner.

#### Build a worker that can recover without buying a second image

Separate submit, poll and download into different steps. The submit worker is the only part that authorizes payment; the poller receives an existing job ID and cannot start another render. For a dashboard, send your own internal request ID to the browser and proxy status through your application. The public poll route itself needs no payment, so treat the job ID and status URL as private references.

1. **Prepare:** authenticate your user, validate the body against the published schema, and save an internal request ID, exact body, target URL, one server-generated idempotency key, and the approved spending cap. Use a unique database constraint or worker lease so a double-click cannot cause two simultaneous renders.
2. **Authorize:** fetch the challenge and compare it to policy. If the requested price exceeds the cap or the resource, chain, token or recipient differs from your allowlist, stop before signing. Record the rail, amount and decision, not the signed authorization itself.
3. **Submit:** use the approved payment client and persist `jobId`, `pollUrl` and any available non-secret payment reference before releasing the worker lease. If the paid request times out before returning a job, record an ambiguous submit. Do not silently start a second paid request or mint another authorization.
4. **Reconcile:** look for the original job and settlement using your payment client or provider records. Use the same request body and `X-Idempotency-Key` for any authorized replay within the documented caching window; the key is not an exactly-once billing guarantee. Escalate when you cannot establish what happened rather than automatically buying another image.
5. **Finish:** poll with a timeout per GET, bounded backoff and a separate overall deadline. Record transitions, keep the job attached when your deadline expires, and resume the GET later if needed. At completion, download and validate the file before marking it ready.

```
# Worker pseudocode: payment/client and storage are your adapters.
row = load_and_lease(request_id)
if row.job_id:
    schedule_poll(row.job_id)
elif row.state in ("submitting", "ambiguous_submit"):
    schedule_reconciliation(row.id)
else:
    terms = get_unpaid_challenge(row.url, row.body)
    require_policy_match(terms, row.approved_cap)
    persist_state(row.id, "submitting")
    try:
        reply = authorized_post_once(row.url, row.body, row.key, terms)
    except TransportError:
        persist_state(row.id, "ambiguous_submit")
    else:
        if reply.http_status == 202 and valid_job_reference(reply):
            persist_job_and_schedule_poll(row.id, reply)
        else:
            record_response_for_classification(row.id, reply)
```

Write the submitting state before the paid network call. If the worker crashes between payment and saving the response, a replacement worker will reconcile rather than assume the job was never submitted. Do not accept arbitrary polling URLs from a browser or follow cross-origin redirects with a payment header.

#### State transitions and failure decisions

| Signal | Client transition | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unsigned POST returns `402` | Awaiting authorization | Evaluate the challenge; no job exists merely because terms were offered. |
| Authorized POST returns `202` and a job reference | Queued | Save the job and poll. Do not resubmit while waiting. |
| GET reports `queued` or `processing` | In progress | Schedule another GET. If your deadline expires, resume later using the same reference. |
| GET reports `completed` with `imageUrl` | Asset available | Fetch, decode and inspect the file before delivery. If download alone fails, retry the download, not generation. |
| GET reports `failed` | Terminal render failure | Keep the job and error for support and reconcile payment separately. An unknown ID can also return this status with HTTP `200`; first check that the ID was preserved correctly. |
| HTTP `400` or `422` | Invalid request | Read the error, correct input or version, and treat a changed render body as a new intent. Validate locally before authorizing payment. |
| `402` after attaching payment | Authorization not accepted | Inspect the challenge and retry hint. Check expiration, network and rail configuration. Do not loop signing new authorizations. |
| Poll GET returns `402` with `payment_required` | Payment not verified for this job | Stop and reconcile the original payment; do not attach a new payment to the GET. |
| HTTP `429` | Throttled | Honor `Retry-After` when supplied. Retain the job if there is one; keep polling and spending retries separate. |
| Network timeout or `5xx` on paid POST | Potentially ambiguous submit | Reconcile before authorizing a replacement. A network error does not tell you whether your request reached the server. |
| Unexpected body, missing URL, or unknown status | Needs investigation | Do not interpret a malformed payload as either a finished asset or permission to pay again. |

#### Translate placement dimensions into a framing choice

`aspectRatio` asks for a shape, not a pixel count. A 1080 × 1920 story slot is 9:16, but requesting 9:16 does not promise that the returned image is exactly 1080 × 1920. Read the actual dimensions after decoding, then crop, pad or resize in your application as needed. These are example placement sizes, not Suede output sizes.

| Placement example | Request ratio | Composition instruction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1080 × 1080 release tile | `1:1` | Keep the sleeve central and reserve space above for a separately typeset title. |
| 1080 × 1350 portrait card | `4:5` | Leave breathing room above and below a person or a tall product. |
| 1080 × 1920 story | `9:16` | Protect the center from captions and interface controls; preview the actual placement. |
| 1920 × 1080 article banner | `16:9` | Keep the subject to one side if the headline will sit on the opposite side. |
| 2100 × 900 wide masthead | `21:9` | Keep important details near the vertical center and away from either edge. |

A centered 9:16 crop of a square source keeps the middle 56.25% of its width if it keeps the full height. If the sleeve fills 75% of the original width, that crop cannot retain it. Padding preserves the whole original at the cost of spare space; a new portrait render can recompose the scene, but it costs another call and may not match the first image. CSS `object-fit: cover` changes what the viewer sees, not the source file. Export a derivative if a downstream platform needs the crop baked in.

For an editorial illustration, brief subject, camera or viewpoint, lighting and empty space. For a product page, keep the actual product photo as the source of truth; use the generated image for concepts or atmosphere rather than treating a generated label, color or shape as the real item. For a storyboard, use one frame per shot and treat continuity between separately generated frames as something to review, not an API guarantee.

#### Turn the hosted image into a usable asset

1. Validate the URL in your downloader. Require HTTPS, enforce your allowed destinations and redirect policy, and do not forward payment credentials. Apply a byte limit and request timeout.
2. Verify the decoded format and dimensions against your delivery needs. A file extension or successful HTTP response does not prove the bytes are a valid PNG or JPEG. Check transparency explicitly if the placement needs it; choosing PNG alone does not request transparency.
3. Keep a controlled original for workflows that need stable storage. Save placement-specific derivatives separately, record the source job ID and requested format, and preserve the original for a future crop. Do not depend on an undocumented retention period.
4. Preview at the actual display size. For visual acceptance, check subject framing, unintended marks or text, the placement of overlays and whether the asset still communicates the brief on a phone. For publishing, add your own text alternative where the image conveys information.

#### Test the full integration with fixtures before a paid smoke test

Use a local HTTP stub or recorded, redacted responses. Assert network calls as well as on-screen state. A status badge can look correct while the client has accidentally submitted a second charge.

| Fixture | Pass condition |
| --- | --- |
| Unsigned `402` for the expected resource | Terms are parsed and displayed; zero paid POSTs are made without approval. |
| Wrong recipient, unsupported network or price above cap | No signing and no paid POST, even if the challenge is otherwise well formed. |
| Two clicks or two workers for one request | One paid submit attempt; both clients resolve to one internal record. |
| `202`, then `processing`, then `completed` | The job survives restart. Only GETs occur after accept, and the decoded file is delivered once. |
| Response dropped after submitting | Request is flagged for reconciliation. Re-running the worker does not sign again. |
| HTTP `200` with `failed`, plus a separate malformed completion | Each is recorded with its own reason; neither is marked delivered or automatically re-rendered. |
| Poll deadline and throttled GET | Backoff respects a retry hint; later resumption uses the same job without a paid POST. |
| Completed response with a bad image or rejected download destination | Asset delivery is blocked and the render remains linked to its original job. |

If you choose to do one real smoke test, authorize one known-valid request at the live terms. Keep evidence of the challenge, accepted job, terminal response, decoded image and payment reference, with credentials removed. Use fixtures for invalid paid requests and ambiguous settlement rather than spending to manufacture failures.

#### Sources

- [app.suedeai.ai/.well-known/x402](https://app.suedeai.ai/.well-known/x402): description, price, payment requirement, input schema and example output (resource entry last updated 2026-08-30).
- [app.suedeai.ai/openapi.json](https://app.suedeai.ai/openapi.json): operations `agent_image` and `agent_image_status`.
- Live requests on 2026-10-11: the unpaid 402 challenge and a poll for an unknown `jobId`.
