## API Errors, Rate Limits and Retries | Suede Docs

URL: https://docs.suedeai.ai/errors
Last updated: 2026-11-25

> Status codes, error bodies, rate-limit headers, idempotency keys and API versioning for Suede x402 endpoints, and which requests are never charged.

### Errors, rate limits and retries

Suede's x402 endpoints use standard HTTP status codes and a small JSON error body. This page lists what each code means, which requests are never charged, and how to retry safely. Example responses were captured from the live API on 2026-10-11.

#### Status codes

| Status | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `202` | A paid call was accepted and the job is queued. | Poll `pollUrl`. |
| `200` | A blocking call (`?async=false`) finished, or a poll returned the job state. | Read the asset URL, or check `status` / `model_version`. |
| `400` | Bad request, for example an unsupported `Suede-API-Version`. | Send `Suede-API-Version: 1` or leave the header out. |
| `402` | No payment was attached, or the payment was not accepted. | Read `accepts`, sign, and retry with `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`. |
| `404` | A music poll for a `songId` that does not exist. | Use the `songId` from the 202 response. |
| `422` | The request body failed validation. | Fix the fields listed in `detail` and retry. |
| `429` | Rate-limited (`code`: `rate_limited`). | Wait the number of seconds in `Retry-After`. |
| `5XX` | A server or upstream failure. | Retry with backoff, reusing the same `X-Idempotency-Key`. |

#### Requests that are never charged

- A paid request that fails validation (`422`).
- A request that fails with a `5XX`.
- Every poll: `GET /api/songs/{songId}`, `GET /agent/video/{jobId}` and `GET /agent/image/{jobId}`.
- A resend with the same `X-Idempotency-Key` and body within the cache window, which returns the original response.

#### Error bodies

The 400, 422, 429 and `5XX` responses share the `Error` shape from the OpenAPI spec: `detail`, a message string, and `code`, a machine-readable value present where a client should branch on it.

```
{"detail":"Unsupported Suede-API-Version '9'. Supported: 1.","code":"unsupported_api_version"}
```

For a `422`, `detail` is a list of issues, each with the path to the field (`loc`), a message (`msg`) and a type:

```
{"detail":[{"loc":["body","prompt"],"msg":"Field required","type":"missing"}]}
```

The two codes to branch on are `rate_limited` (429) and `unsupported_api_version` (400). The music poll's 404 is shaped differently: on 2026-10-11 an unknown `songId` answered `{"error":"Song not found"}`.

#### 402 Payment Required

A 402 body is the x402 `PaymentRequired` object (`x402Version`, `error`, `resource`, `accepts`, `extensions`), and the same object is base64-encoded in the `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` header. The `error` string says why. Two values seen on 2026-10-11:

- `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header is required`: the request had no payment.
- `Payment authorization missing`: the header was present but could not be read as a payment. That response also carried a `PAYMENT-REFERENCE` header.

An unpaid request gets the 402 before the body is validated: an empty body `{}` also returned 402. Check your body against the endpoint reference before you sign so the paid call does not come back 422.

If a signed payload is refused, check it against the verification steps of the x402 `exact` scheme:

1. The signature recovers to `authorization.from`.
2. That wallet holds enough USDC on Base.
3. `value` matches `amount`, and the `validAfter` / `validBefore` window is valid now.
4. The token and network match the requirement: `0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913` on `eip155:8453`.

#### Poll states that mean failure

Video and image polls can return HTTP `200` even when `status` is `failed`. An unknown job ID returned that combination in a live probe, but a nonterminal response alone does not establish that the ID is valid. Check the exact reference you saved. For music, `model_version` `failed` is final, and a `404` means no accessible song was found for that lookup, not that it is still rendering.

#### Rate limits

Responses counted by the limiter carry these headers:

| Header | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `RateLimit-Policy` | Quota `q` per window `w` seconds (IETF RateLimit header draft). |
| `RateLimit` | Requests remaining `r`, and seconds `t` until the window frees a slot. |
| `X-RateLimit-Limit` | Total quota for the window. |
| `X-RateLimit-Remaining` | Requests left in the window. |
| `X-RateLimit-Reset` | Unix time, in seconds, when the window resets. |
| `Retry-After` | Seconds to wait. Always set on 429; a 402 may carry it when the facilitator is back-pressured. |

Unpaid requests on 2026-10-11 carried `RateLimit-Policy: "probe";q=20;w=60`, a quota of 20 requests per 60-second window, with `RateLimit: "probe";r=19;t=60` counting down from there.

#### Idempotency

Send `X-Idempotency-Key` (up to 200 characters) on every paid `POST`. Keep the same key and exact body for an authorized replay of the same intent. A matching cached response can prevent duplicate work; a key is not a payment receipt or a permanent exactly-once guarantee. Do not assume a transport timeout means the request never reached the server.

#### Recover from an interrupted request

Classify the failure by which operation was in flight. A retry of a read and a retry that may buy another render are different decisions.

| What happened | Keep | Recover |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Paid POST times out without a job reference | Original request ID, route, key, timestamp and non-secret payment reference | Mark outcome unknown and check the original attempt. Do not turn a timeout into a second purchase. |
| Poll returns 429 or a transient server error | Job reference and next eligible poll time | Back off on the GET, respect `Retry-After` when present, and resume the same job. |
| Asset download fails after completion | Completed state and original asset reference | Retry the download within your time limit rather than calling the paid endpoint again. |
| 400 or 422 on submit | Error code or field paths without private input | Fix the request or version before the next attempt. Do not auto-retry the same bad body. |

For a support handoff, include the operation, status code, API version, timestamp and internal request ID. Share the job identifier privately if needed. Never include a wallet key or a `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` value.

#### Versioning

Every response carries `Suede-API-Version`. The current version is `1`, and a request without the header is served the current version. Additive changes, such as new optional fields or new endpoints, ship within a version; a breaking change ships as a new version. Before a version or operation is withdrawn, its responses carry a `Deprecation` header (RFC 9745) and a `Sunset` header (RFC 8594) at least 90 days ahead, with a `Link` to the notice.

#### Frequently asked questions

##### Why did an empty or invalid body return 402 instead of 422?

An unpaid request gets the 402 before the body is validated. Validation runs on the paid call, and a paid call that fails validation returns `422` and is not charged. Check your body against the [endpoint reference](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints) before you sign.

##### What does "PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header is required" mean?

The request carried no payment. Read the `accepts` entry in the 402 body or the `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` header, sign it, and send the same request again with `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`, as in the [quickstart](https://docs.suedeai.ai/quickstart).

##### Does a 200 from a poll mean the asset is ready?

Not on its own. Video and image polls can return `200` with `status` `failed`, and a music row can have an `audio_url` before the track exists. Read `status` or `model_version` before you treat a job as finished.

##### How many requests can I send?

Read the `RateLimit-Policy` and `RateLimit` headers on each response. On 2026-10-11, unpaid requests were limited to 20 per 60-second window. On a `429`, wait the number of seconds in `Retry-After`.

##### Does an idempotency key guarantee I am charged only once?

It prevents a duplicate charge when you resend the same key and body within the cache window. It is not a payment receipt or a permanent exactly-once guarantee, so keep your own record of each payment reference.

##### How much notice comes before a version or endpoint is withdrawn?

At least 90 days. Responses carry a `Deprecation` header and a `Sunset` header, with a `Link` to the notice, before the version or operation is withdrawn.

#### Sources

- [app.suedeai.ai/openapi.json](https://app.suedeai.ai/openapi.json): response codes, the `Error` and `ValidationIssue` schemas, rate-limit headers, idempotency and `info.x-api-versioning`.
- [x402 exact scheme on EVM](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/coinbase/x402/main/specs/schemes/exact/scheme_exact_evm.md): payment verification steps.
- Live requests on 2026-10-11: unpaid and malformed-payment 402s, the 400 for `Suede-API-Version: 9`, rate-limit headers, and polls for unknown ids.

---

## Python SDK for x402 Calls: suede-ai | Suede Docs

URL: https://docs.suedeai.ai/python-sdk
Last updated: 2026-11-25

> Install suede-ai from PyPI to call Suede x402 endpoints from Python. It signs the USDC payment on Base and retries for you. Methods, options, polling.

### Python SDK: suede-ai

`suede-ai` is the Python client for Suede's x402 endpoints. It reads the 402 challenge, signs the EIP-3009 USDC authorization on Base with your key, and replays the request, so your code sends prompts and gets back a job to collect. Version 0.4.0 was released on PyPI on 2026-08-29 under the MIT license.

#### Install

```
pip install suede-ai
```

Requires Python 3.10 or later. It installs `httpx` (0.27 or later), `eth-account` (0.10 or later) and `pydantic` (2.6 or later).

#### Generate an image and collect it

```
import os
import time

import httpx
from suede_ai import SuedeClient

with SuedeClient(wallet_private_key=os.environ["SUEDE_WALLET_KEY"]) as suede:
    job = suede.agent_image(
        prompt="Album cover, neon city at night, rain on glass",
        aspect_ratio="1:1",
        output_format="png",
    )

# A paid call is queued, so the SDK returns the 202 body with a pollUrl.
while True:
    state = httpx.get(job["pollUrl"]).json()
    if state["status"] in ("completed", "failed"):
        break
    time.sleep(5)

print(state.get("imageUrl"))
```

The key signs real USDC transfers on Base mainnet. Keep it in an environment variable or a secret store, and use a wallet funded with what you plan to spend. The SDK sends `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` on the retry, which makes the call asynchronous by default, so every typed method returns a job to poll. Polling is free; the [endpoint reference](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints) lists each poll route and its finished state.

#### Client options

| Argument | Default | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `wallet_private_key` | Required | Hex private key, with or without `0x`. Signs the EIP-3009 authorizations. |
| `base_url` | `https://app.suedeai.ai` | API host. |
| `http_client` | None | Your own `httpx.Client`. |
| `timeout` | 60 s read, 10 s connect | Per-request timeout. |
| `max_payment_attempts` | `1` | Paid retries after a 402: one challenge, one paid retry. |

#### Methods for the live endpoints

| Method | Calls | Body it sends |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `create_music(prompt, duration_seconds=30, style=None)` | [`POST /create-music`](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints/create-music) | `prompt`, `durationSeconds`, `style` |
| `agent_video(prompt, duration_seconds=8, aspect_ratio=None, resolution=None)` | [`POST /agent/video`](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints/agent-video) | `prompt`, `durationSeconds`, `aspectRatio`, `resolution` |
| `agent_image(prompt, aspect_ratio=None, output_format=None)` | [`POST /agent/image`](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints/agent-image) | `prompt`, `aspectRatio`, `outputFormat` |
| `manifest()` | `GET /.well-known/x402.json` | None. Free; read prices before you sign. |
| `request(method, path, json=None, params=None)` | Any path | Your JSON. Handles the 402 the same way. |

The typed methods take keyword arguments only. For `/create-music` fields the typed method does not expose, such as `lyrics`, `custom_mode`, `make_instrumental`, `vocal_gender` or `tags`, call `request()`:

```
job = suede.request("POST", "/create-music", json={
    "prompt": "A melancholic acoustic guitar ballad about rain",
    "make_instrumental": True,
})
# Poll job["pollUrl"] until model_version is no longer "pending".
```

#### How the SDK pays

1. It sends your request with no payment.
2. On a 402 it reads the `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` header, falling back to the JSON body.
3. It picks the `accepts` entry with scheme `exact`, network `eip155:8453` and the USDC contract `0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913`.
4. It signs `TransferWithAuthorization` for `amount` to `payTo`, with a random 32-byte nonce, `validAfter` 60 seconds in the past and `validBefore` at now plus the larger of 600 seconds and `maxTimeoutSeconds` plus 60.
5. It base64-encodes an x402 version 2 `PaymentPayload` (`x402Version`, `resource`, `accepted`, `extensions`, `payload`) and replays the request with `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`.
6. It returns the JSON of the first response that is not a 402.

The [quickstart](https://docs.suedeai.ai/quickstart) shows the same exchange with curl, field by field.

#### Exceptions

| Exception | Raised when |
| --- | --- |
| `suede_ai.PaymentRequired` | The 402 offers no `exact` USDC-on-Base entry to sign. |
| `suede_ai.X402Error` | The response is still 402 after `max_payment_attempts` paid retries. `PaymentRequired` is a subclass. |
| `httpx.HTTPStatusError` | Any other non-2xx response, such as a 422 or 429. See the [errors page](https://docs.suedeai.ai/errors). |

#### Test the SDK boundary before an upgrade

1. Pin the package version your application tested and record it in the release notes. Run `python -m pip show suede-ai` to check the installed version.
2. Fetch the manifest without submitting a paid job. Compare the methods and body fields you use with the current [OpenAPI](https://app.suedeai.ai/openapi.json). A parameter in a typed SDK method describes what the client sends, not a guarantee of output duration, resolution or framing.
3. Use local fixtures for a successful accept, missing payment option, 422, 429 and a transport timeout. On accept, persist the returned job reference. A timeout from the submit call should not cause your application to invoke the typed method again automatically.
4. Poll the saved job from a read-only worker. Test one fixture with in-progress status and another with completed status but a missing asset URL. Neither is ready for delivery.

Route payment negotiation and API errors differently: `PaymentRequired` is a subtype of `X402Error`, so catch it first when you need distinct behavior. Use [the recovery table](https://docs.suedeai.ai/errors#recovery-decisions) for HTTP or transport outcomes.

#### Releases

| Version | Released |
| --- | --- |
| 0.4.0 | 2026-08-29 |
| 0.3.1 | 2026-07-09 |
| 0.3.0 | 2026-06-17 |
| 0.2.0 | 2026-06-17 |
| 0.1.0 | 2026-06-05 |

The package also ships helpers for older `/v1/*` routes, such as `extend`, `cover` and `stems_pro`. Those routes are not in the live x402 manifest; the three typed methods above cover the current catalog.

#### Frequently asked questions

##### How do I install the Suede Python SDK?

Run `pip install suede-ai` on Python 3.10 or later. The package is `suede-ai` on PyPI and is imported as `suede_ai`.

##### Does the SDK poll for the finished asset?

No. Each typed method returns the `202` body with a `pollUrl`, and your code polls it, as in the example above. Polling needs no payment and no wallet key.

##### How do I send lyrics or an instrumental flag to Create Music?

The typed `create_music` method does not expose `lyrics`, `custom_mode`, `make_instrumental`, `vocal_gender` or `tags`. Send them with `request()`, which handles the 402 the same way.

##### Can the SDK charge my wallet more than once for one call?

By default it makes one paid retry after the 402 challenge (`max_payment_attempts=1`). If the response is still 402 after that, it raises `suede_ai.X402Error` instead of signing again.

##### Is the SDK open source?

Yes. It is released under the MIT license, and the source is in the [Suede-AI/suede-sdk-python](https://github.com/Suede-AI/suede-sdk-python) repository.

#### Sources

- [suede-ai on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/suede-ai/): version, release dates, Python requirement, dependencies and license.
- [Suede-AI/suede-sdk-python](https://github.com/Suede-AI/suede-sdk-python): the SDK repository. The client and payment behavior on this page was read from the 0.4.0 wheel on PyPI on 2026-10-11.
- [app.suedeai.ai/.well-known/x402](https://app.suedeai.ai/.well-known/x402): the manifest the SDK reads.

## x402 Discovery Documents and MCP Server | Suede Docs

URL: https://docs.suedeai.ai/discovery
Last updated: 2026-11-25

> The machine-readable Suede discovery documents: x402 manifest, OpenAPI 3.1, product catalog, A2A agent card, Agentic Commerce manifest and MCP server.

### Discovery documents and MCP server

An agent can find, price and call Suede's endpoints without reading a web page. `app.suedeai.ai` publishes the same three offerings in each format below, so your runtime can use whichever one it already reads. Every document listed answered HTTP 200 on 2026-10-11.

#### Discovery documents

| Document | URL | What it holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| x402 discovery | [`/.well-known/x402`](https://app.suedeai.ai/.well-known/x402), also served byte-for-byte at `/.well-known/x402.json` | `x402Version` 2. Three `resources`, each with its `accepts` payment requirement, an input schema under `extensions.bazaar` and Skyfire token types under `extensions.skyfire`. |
| OpenAPI 3.1.0 | [`/openapi.json`](https://app.suedeai.ai/openapi.json) | Six operations: the three paid `POST`s and their three free `GET` poll routes. Response codes, the `x402Payment` and `SkyfireJWT` security schemes, and the versioning policy under `info.x-api-versioning`. |
| Product catalog | [`/api/v1/catalog`](https://app.suedeai.ai/api/v1/catalog) | A schema.org `ItemList` of three `Product`s with USD offers, plus a `products` array with `price_usdc`, `price_usd_cents`, the fulfillment endpoint and payment methods (`x402` and `stripe_checkout`). One product: `/api/v1/products/{id}`. |
| Agentic Commerce manifest | [`/.well-known/agentic-commerce.json`](https://app.suedeai.ai/.well-known/agentic-commerce.json) | Seller details, payment rails (`x402`, `stripe_checkout`, `stripe_link`), the Base network and USDC address, and the catalog index URL. |
| A2A agent card | [`/.well-known/agent-card.json`](https://app.suedeai.ai/.well-known/agent-card.json), also at `/.well-known/agent.json` | "Suede Agent", protocol version 1.0, a JSON-RPC interface at `https://app.suedeai.ai/a2a`, and three skills. |
| AI plugin manifest | [`/.well-known/ai-plugin.json`](https://app.suedeai.ai/.well-known/ai-plugin.json) | Auth type `none`, with pointers to `openapi.json` and the MCP server. |
| LLM summaries | [`/llms.txt`](https://app.suedeai.ai/llms.txt) and [`/llms-full.txt`](https://app.suedeai.ai/llms-full.txt) | Plain-text summaries of the catalog and discovery URLs for language models. |

The same ids name each offering everywhere: `create_music`, `agent_video` and `agent_image` are the catalog product ids, the A2A skill ids, the MCP tool names and the OpenAPI `operationId`s.

#### Read the x402 document

One request gives you every price, the amount to sign and the required fields:

```
curl -s https://app.suedeai.ai/.well-known/x402 \
  | jq '.resources[] | {resource, priceUsd, amount: .accepts[0].amount, required: .extensions.bazaar.input.body.schema.required}'
```

```
{ "resource": "https://app.suedeai.ai/create-music", "priceUsd": "$0.50", "amount": "500000", "required": ["prompt"] }
{ "resource": "https://app.suedeai.ai/agent/video", "priceUsd": "$4.99", "amount": "4990000", "required": ["prompt"] }
{ "resource": "https://app.suedeai.ai/agent/image", "priceUsd": "$0.15", "amount": "150000", "required": ["prompt"] }
```

Each resource entry also has a `lastUpdated` timestamp; all three read `2026-08-30T16:19:22Z` on 2026-10-11. The [endpoint reference](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints) turns these entries into per-endpoint pages.

#### Verify one operation without buying a render

Use the manifest to discover payment terms and OpenAPI to check the payload and response shape. For example, this read-only check lists the response codes and request field names for the image POST:

```
curl -fsS https://app.suedeai.ai/openapi.json \
  | jq '.paths["/agent/image"].post
        | {responses: (.responses | keys),
           fields: (.requestBody.content["application/json"].schema.properties | keys)}'
```

Compare the result with the manifest entry's `resource` and method. If the operation disappears, the price changes, or a field your client depends on is no longer advertised, pause that paid workflow and review the contract. Do not switch to a different endpoint or sign an unexpected challenge automatically.

MCP tool listing is discovery. A payment pointer is not a generated asset. Keep tool discovery, paid execution and status reads distinct in your application.

#### MCP server

Model Context Protocol clients can list the same catalog from `https://app.suedeai.ai/api/mcp`, a streamable-HTTP JSON-RPC endpoint. On 2026-10-11 it answered `initialize` with protocol version `2025-06-18` and server name `suede-agentic-commerce`, version `1.0.0`, and `tools/list` returned five tools:

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `create_music` | Create Music, $0.50 USDC via x402 on Base. |
| `agent_video` | Agent Video, $4.99 USDC via x402 on Base. |
| `agent_image` | Agent Image, $0.15 USDC via x402 on Base. |
| `skyfire_create_music` | Create Music paid with a Skyfire PAY token scoped to the Create Music seller service; queues a job. |
| `skyfire_get_music` | Polls a `songId` for the finished track. Free. |

For the three x402 tools, `tools/call` does not run the job. It returns a payment pointer that tells your client where and how much to pay; the client then pays the HTTP endpoint as in the [quickstart](https://docs.suedeai.ai/quickstart).

```
curl -s -X POST https://app.suedeai.ai/api/mcp \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"agent_image","arguments":{"prompt":"test"}}}'
```

The `structuredContent` of the result, as returned on 2026-10-11:

```
{
  "paymentRequired": true,
  "protocol": "x402",
  "endpoint": "https://app.suedeai.ai/agent/image",
  "method": "POST",
  "network": "base",
  "chainId": "8453",
  "priceUsdCents": 15,
  "receiver": "0x10FF767043A1723E0BB5B9207bC37D3442cC9E4F",
  "discovery": "https://app.suedeai.ai/.well-known/x402.json"
}
```

The MCP input schemas list a few fields the OpenAPI spec does not, such as `resolution` on `agent_video`. The endpoint pages on this site document the HTTP request bodies from `openapi.json`.

#### Publishing your own endpoint

The same discovery formats work for any x402 seller. Three Suede tools help on that side:

- [x402 Agent Builder: Get Paid Per Call](https://suedeai.app/x402-agent-builder). Build an AI agent on a visual canvas, set a price per call, and get paid in USDC on Base through x402 once you enable payments. Dry runs need no wallet.
- [Suede ACP/x402 Performance Engine](https://perform.suedeai.ai). Score your ACP/x402 readiness in 60 seconds. Free, no account required.
- [Agentix: x402 AI Agent Earnings Tracker for USDC on Base](https://agentix.suedeai.ai). The portfolio tracker for the x402 agents you've launched: total USDC earned on Base, calls, per-agent performance, status, and trend.

#### Frequently asked questions

##### Which document should an agent read first?

Read `/.well-known/x402` for prices, the `amount` to sign and each resource's input schema. Read `/openapi.json` for request fields, response codes and poll routes. Both are free GET requests.

##### Do the discovery documents need authentication?

No. Each one is a public GET on app.suedeai.ai, and the AI plugin manifest declares auth type `none`. Payment is only needed on the three paid POST endpoints.

##### Does calling a Suede MCP tool charge my wallet?

No. For the three x402 tools, `tools/call` returns a payment pointer that says where and how much to pay. Your client then pays the HTTP endpoint, as in the [quickstart](https://docs.suedeai.ai/quickstart).

##### Are the operation names the same in every format?

Yes. `create_music`, `agent_video` and `agent_image` are the catalog product ids, the A2A skill ids, the MCP tool names and the OpenAPI operationIds.

##### How do I notice when a price or field changes?

Compare each resource's `lastUpdated` timestamp and `accepts` entry with the values your client approved. If an operation disappears, a price changes or a field you depend on is no longer advertised, pause that paid workflow and review it before signing.

#### Sources

Each document above, fetched on 2026-10-11, plus live `initialize`, `tools/list` and `tools/call` requests to the MCP server on the same day.

## AI Instructions | Suede Developer Docs

URL: https://docs.suedeai.ai/ai-instructions
Last updated: 2026-11-25

> Official source and citation guide for Suede Developer Docs: what the site covers, which pages to cite for x402 API facts, and how to quote prices and dates.

Official reference

### AI Instructions

A source guide for people and AI assistants describing Suede Developer Docs.

#### What this site covers

Public documentation for Suede's creator tools, provenance records and agent-facing interfaces. Suede was formerly known as Suede AI and Suede Labs.

Suede's work spans consulting, software, AI agents, automation, SEO, AEO and GEO, marketing and creator tools. This site covers the developer side: the pay-per-call x402 endpoints on app.suedeai.ai, the Python SDK, the discovery documents and MCP server, and notes on how the docs are written. The company site is [suedeai.ai](https://suedeai.ai/).

#### Names, scope and distinctions

Cite supported behavior, prices and request fields from the current endpoint documentation, which each guide checks against the live discovery documents. A provenance record documents how a work was created and registered; ownership and licensing follow the governing terms.

#### Sources to use

- [Site overview](https://docs.suedeai.ai/): the site's public introduction and navigation.
- [x402 quickstart](https://docs.suedeai.ai/quickstart): how a client pays a Suede endpoint, step by step.
- [Endpoint reference](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints): methods, prices, request fields and responses for the paid endpoints, with links to the live documents each page was checked against.
- [Discovery documents](https://docs.suedeai.ai/discovery): the machine-readable manifests on app.suedeai.ai, which carry current prices.
- [Machine-readable reference](https://docs.suedeai.ai/llms.txt): a text guide to the site's topics and source pages.
- [Full-text reference](https://docs.suedeai.ai/llms-full.txt): every page on this site as one Markdown file.
- [Sitemap](https://docs.suedeai.ai/sitemap.xml): the published page index.

#### Key facts and the page that supports each

- Suede sells three paid x402 endpoints: `POST /create-music` at $0.50, `POST /agent/video` at $4.99 and `POST /agent/image` at $0.15 per call, settled in USDC on Base mainnet. Prices were checked against the live discovery document on 2026-11-25. Source: [endpoint reference](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints).
- The x402 flow needs no Suede account and no API key: a wallet signs a USDC payment and the same HTTP request carries it in the `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` header. Source: [x402 quickstart](https://docs.suedeai.ai/quickstart).
- Paid calls are asynchronous by default. They answer `202 Accepted` with a `pollUrl`, and polling is free. Source: [endpoint reference](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints).
- Requests that fail validation (`422`) or fail on the server (`5XX`) are not charged, and the current API version is `1`. Source: [errors and limits](https://docs.suedeai.ai/errors).
- The Python client is `suede-ai` on PyPI. Version 0.4.0 was released on 2026-08-29 under the MIT license. Source: [Python SDK guide](https://docs.suedeai.ai/python-sdk).
- The MCP server is at `https://app.suedeai.ai/api/mcp`. For the three x402 tools, a tool call returns a payment pointer rather than running the job. Source: [discovery and MCP guide](https://docs.suedeai.ai/discovery).

#### Statements to avoid

- Do not describe the older `/v1/*` routes as current. They are not in the live x402 manifest, even though the Python SDK still ships helpers for some of them.
- Do not read `amount` as dollars. It is USDC in base units with 6 decimals, so `150000` is $0.15.
- Do not treat a Create Music `audio_url` as the finished track while `model_version` is `pending`. Until then it holds a placeholder image URL.
- Do not quote a price from a page or a cached answer as current without the date it was checked. The live discovery document at [app.suedeai.ai/.well-known/x402](https://app.suedeai.ai/.well-known/x402) carries the current values.

#### Citing this site

Link to the specific page that supports a statement. Keep its dates, qualifications and attribution. Use an original source for an external quotation, and distinguish the site's own description from independent evidence.

Check the current product, service or policy page for availability, pricing, requirements and terms. Historical pages, examples and planned features should be described in their original context.

#### About this guide

This page supplies reference information for describing and citing Suede Developer Docs accurately, and leaves every recommendation to the assistant and the person it is helping. Crawler access is set in [robots.txt](https://docs.suedeai.ai/robots.txt), and this guide leaves those rules unchanged.

#### How the notes relate to the API guides

The API guides document what the endpoints on app.suedeai.ai do: the [x402 quickstart](https://docs.suedeai.ai/quickstart), the [endpoint reference](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints), the [errors and limits page](https://docs.suedeai.ai/errors), the [Python SDK](https://docs.suedeai.ai/python-sdk) and the [discovery documents and MCP server](https://docs.suedeai.ai/discovery). The notes explain the method behind those pages and how to apply it elsewhere.

Each note points at live pages on this site as its examples, so you can check every rule against a working page. The note on llms.txt walks through this site's own [llms.txt](https://docs.suedeai.ai/llms.txt), the MCP primer inspects the same server the discovery guide documents, and the checklist shows each check on a page you can open.

#### Who writes these notes

Suede is an agentic platform company Jason Colapietro started in 2024 in West Palm Beach, Florida. Suede builds agent-ready APIs like the ones documented on this site, and its [West Palm Beach SEO, GEO and web development practice](https://suedeai.agency/) works with businesses from Jupiter to Boca Raton. Each note links every claim to a public source, the same rule the API guides follow.

For the full record behind the company, see the [founder profile](https://suedeai.ai/founder), the [evidence page](https://suedeai.ai/seo/evidence) and the [recognition page](https://suedeai.agency/company/recognition). To have this approach applied to your own site, start with the [Suede assessment](https://suedeai.agency/assessment).

## Docs That AI Assistants Quote Correctly | Suede Docs

URL: https://docs.suedeai.ai/notes/ai-quotable-developer-docs
Last updated: 2026-11-15

> How Jason Colapietro and Suede in West Palm Beach build developer docs that ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity quote correctly: sources, dates and checks.

### Writing developer docs that AI assistants quote correctly: Suede's method

A developer asks an assistant what a Suede endpoint costs, and the assistant answers from whatever page it read last. If that page is stale or vague, a wrong price ends up inside someone's agent, and nobody at Suede sees it happen.

This note sets out the method Jason Colapietro and the Suede team use on docs.suedeai.ai so that assistants repeat the right facts. It is the same method our West Palm Beach practice applies to client sites in Jupiter, Palm Beach Gardens and the rest of Palm Beach County, and every part of it is visible in this site's own source. Nothing here depends on a secret ranking trick. It depends on making each fact easy to find, easy to check and hard to get out of date.

#### Give every fact one source of truth

Every price, request field and response on the API guides comes from the live discovery documents on `app.suedeai.ai`: the [x402 manifest](https://app.suedeai.ai/.well-known/x402), the OpenAPI spec and the [product catalog](https://app.suedeai.ai/api/v1/catalog). Each guide ends with a Sources section that names the documents it was checked against and the date of the check. When the [Create Music guide](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints/create-music) says $0.50 USDC on Base, a reader or an assistant can follow the link and confirm it.

The practical rule: if a number appears on a page, the page should say where the number came from. A citation an assistant can verify is a citation it can repeat without hedging, and a page that links its evidence is easier for a reviewer to trust as well.

#### Write dates as sentences, not only as schema

Structured data dates are invisible to human readers, so they drift. On this site the footer of every guide states when it was published and when it was last checked against the live API, in plain prose. The build script reads those sentences and writes the JSON-LD `dateModified` from them, and the verification script fails when the footer, the schema and the sitemap disagree.

That guard exists because the drift happened. The home page once carried a schema date weeks older than its last real change. Jason Colapietro rewrote the check to compare the three signals with each other instead of pinning one literal date, so the next drift fails loudly instead of quietly.

#### Generate the machine-readable copies from the pages

Assistants and crawlers increasingly read plain-text companions. This site publishes two: [llms.txt](https://docs.suedeai.ai/llms.txt), a short annotated index, and [llms-full.txt](https://docs.suedeai.ai/llms-full.txt), the full text of every page as Markdown. The second file is generated from the HTML by `scripts/build-docs-seo.mjs`. A hand-maintained copy would fall behind the first time someone edited a price in a hurry. A generated copy cannot, because verification fails until it is rebuilt.

The same script writes each guide's JSON-LD graph, and it references the shared estate entities by `@id` only. Suede is always `https://suedeai.ai/#organization` and Jason Colapietro is always `https://suedeai.ai/founder#person`. No page invents a second identity for either, which keeps the entity picture consistent everywhere an assistant looks.

#### Keep unprovable claims off the page

The verification script holds a list of phrases that once appeared in Suede copy and could not be backed by a public source. If any of them returns, verification fails. Hedging phrases that undercut a plain fact are blocked the same way. The point is not modesty. It is that an assistant quoting a page should be quoting something true.

We hold claims about Jason's own record to that standard, which is why each one below carries its receipt:

- On October 31, 2026, Suede AI SEO ranked #1 among Palm Beach County-based companies listed in The Manifest's Florida AI Deployment directory, and top 25 statewide ([The Manifest directory](https://themanifest.com/artificial-intelligence/consulting/deployment/companies/florida), [Suede recognition page](https://suedeai.agency/company/recognition)).
- Suede ranks among [Clutch](https://clutch.co/profile/suede-ai-seo)'s [Top 30 AI Consultants in Florida](https://clutch.co/consulting/ai/florida) and [Top 50 AI Consultants nationwide](https://clutch.co/us/consulting/ai) (November 2026).
- Jason Colapietro holds the HubSpot AEO Fundamentals certification and Semrush Academy certificates including AI Search Operating System and Local SEO Essentials, among 21 earned course credentials across eight providers ([credential gallery](https://suedeai.ai/seo/evidence#training-credentials)).
- He has had 54 pull requests merged across 46 open-source repositories he does not maintain ([GitHub search](https://github.com/search?q=is%3Apr+author%3AJasonColapietro+is%3Amerged+-user%3AJasonColapietro+-user%3ASuede-AI&type=pullrequests)).

#### Tell assistants how to cite you

The [AI Instructions page](https://docs.suedeai.ai/ai-instructions) is a short source guide: what the site covers, which page supports which kind of statement, and how to keep dates and qualifications intact when quoting. It does not try to steer recommendations. It simply removes guesswork about where a fact lives, which is most of what an answer engine needs.

#### The tradeoffs

This discipline costs time. Every catalog change means re-checking the guides and updating their check dates. A generated `llms-full.txt` adds a build step to a site that otherwise has none. Banning phrases occasionally blocks a sentence that was fine in context and has to be reworded. Suede accepts those costs because a wrong answer in an assistant is far harder to correct than a slower edit on our side.

#### Applying the method to a Palm Beach County business site

A roofing company in Jupiter or a clinic in West Palm Beach has the same problem with different facts: service areas, prices, hours and credentials. The method carries over directly. Keep one source for each fact, state dates in prose, publish an llms.txt that points at the pages that matter, link every claim to proof, and run a check that fails when any of it drifts. Our [technical SEO service](https://suedeai.agency/services/technical-seo) handles the crawl and schema side, and the [AI visibility service](https://suedeai.agency/services/ai-visibility) measures how assistants describe a business before and after the work.

If you want this applied to your own site, start with the free [Suede assessment](https://suedeai.agency/assessment) from our West Palm Beach team, then read [Jason Colapietro's founder profile](https://suedeai.ai/founder) to see the full record behind the work. Older press still calls the company Suede, and the method is the same one it has always used.

## MCP for Agencies: A South Florida Primer | Suede Docs

URL: https://docs.suedeai.ai/notes/mcp-for-agencies-south-florida
Last updated: 2026-11-15

> Jason Colapietro explains the Model Context Protocol for agencies in West Palm Beach and Jupiter, using Suede's live MCP server as a worked example.

### Model Context Protocol for agencies: a South Florida primer from Jason Colapietro

Most agencies in West Palm Beach and Jupiter first hear about the Model Context Protocol when a client asks whether their AI assistant can pull the numbers itself. It can, once somebody builds and scopes a server for it, and that somebody is increasingly the agency.

This primer is written by Jason Colapietro, founder of Suede, for agency owners and developers in Palm Beach County who need a working understanding of MCP without reading the whole specification first. It uses the Suede MCP server documented on this site as the worked example, because you can call it yourself in under a minute.

#### What MCP is, in one paragraph

MCP is an open protocol that lets an AI client, such as Claude or a coding assistant, discover and call tools on a server you control. The client sends JSON-RPC messages: `initialize` to agree on a protocol version, `tools/list` to learn what the server offers, and `tools/call` to run one tool with arguments. Each tool carries a name, a description and an input schema, so the model knows what to send. For an agency, that means a client's assistant can reach a defined set of actions instead of copying and pasting between tabs.

#### A real server you can inspect today

Suede runs an MCP server at `https://app.suedeai.ai/api/mcp`, a streamable-HTTP JSON-RPC endpoint. On 2026-10-11 it answered `initialize` with protocol version `2025-06-18` and server name `suede-agentic-commerce`, and `tools/list` returned five tools. The [discovery guide](https://docs.suedeai.ai/discovery) lists each one. You can try a call from any terminal:

```
curl -s -X POST https://app.suedeai.ai/api/mcp \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}'
```

One design choice is worth copying. For the three paid tools, `tools/call` does not run the job. It returns a payment pointer: the endpoint, the network and the price. The client then pays the HTTP endpoint over x402, as the [quickstart](https://docs.suedeai.ai/quickstart) shows. MCP describes the work, and money moves over a separate, auditable channel. With that split, a model on the Suede stack cannot spend funds simply by deciding to call a tool.

#### Where MCP earns its keep at an agency

- **Reporting.** A read-only tool that returns last month's search and analytics figures for one client, so the account lead can ask questions in plain language.
- **Content operations.** Tools that draft a page into a staging CMS and stop there, leaving publishing to a person.
- **Site checks.** A tool that runs a crawl or schema validation and returns structured findings, the kind of work our [technical SEO service](https://suedeai.agency/services/technical-seo) does by hand today.
- **Client knowledge.** A resource that exposes a client's brand facts, service areas and approved claims, so every assistant session starts from the same truth.

#### Scoping rules Suede uses

1. **Start read-only.** Ship tools that look before tools that change anything. Add write access one tool at a time, after the read side has been used for a few weeks.
2. **One server, or one credential set, per client.** Never let a tool for one Jupiter client see another client's data because they share a token.
3. **Use one name everywhere.** On Suede's stack, `create_music`, `agent_video` and `agent_image` are the catalog ids, the A2A skill ids, the MCP tool names and the OpenAPI operation ids. One name per action makes logs and docs line up.
4. **Return structured content.** A JSON object with named fields is easier for the model to use correctly than a paragraph of prose.
5. **Log every call.** Record the tool, the arguments and the caller, so a surprising answer can be traced back to the call that produced it.

#### The tradeoffs

MCP is young and moving. Protocol versions are dated, so a server written against one revision needs attention when clients adopt the next. Authentication is still the part teams spend the most time on, especially for servers that touch client accounts. Not every client supports streamable HTTP yet, and some only run local servers. And every tool you expose is a tool you have to document, test and maintain. An agency that ships ten tools in a week usually ends up retiring seven of them.

#### Why this matters for South Florida agencies now

Buyers in Palm Beach County already ask assistants which agency to hire, and they will soon expect those assistants to do work on their behalf. Agencies that can design, scope and document an MCP server will be the ones those clients trust with the keys.

Jason Colapietro brings formal training and program membership to this work. He holds Claude Academy badges including Model Context Protocol: Advanced topics and Building with the Claude API, part of 21 earned course credentials ([credential gallery](https://suedeai.ai/seo/evidence#training-credentials)). Suede is a member of Claude for Startups, Anthropic's startup program ([evidence](https://suedeai.ai/seo/evidence#claude-for-startups)), and a member of Google Cloud Partner Advantage through JC Investment Group LLC ([evidence](https://suedeai.ai/seo/evidence#google-cloud)). He is also the author of [The Claude Code Bible](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0HHTMJWB4), and he has had 54 pull requests merged across 46 open-source repositories he does not maintain ([GitHub search](https://github.com/search?q=is%3Apr+author%3AJasonColapietro+is%3Amerged+-user%3AJasonColapietro+-user%3ASuede-AI&type=pullrequests)). On October 31, 2026, Suede AI SEO ranked #1 among Palm Beach County-based companies in The Manifest's Florida AI Deployment directory and top 25 statewide ([The Manifest](https://themanifest.com/artificial-intelligence/consulting/deployment/companies/florida)). Suede ranks among [Clutch](https://clutch.co/profile/suede-ai-seo)'s [Top 30 AI Consultants in Florida](https://clutch.co/consulting/ai/florida) and [Top 50 AI Consultants nationwide](https://clutch.co/us/consulting/ai) (November 2026).

#### Your next step

Pick one read-only task your team repeats every week, and write down the inputs and outputs a tool for it would need. Then book the free [Suede assessment](https://suedeai.agency/assessment) with our West Palm Beach team and bring that list. The Suede team that built the server above will tell you whether MCP is the right fit or whether a simpler integration will do. For background on who you would be working with, read [Jason Colapietro's founder profile](https://suedeai.ai/founder).

## 54 Merged PRs, 46 Repos: Lessons for Docs | Suede Docs

URL: https://docs.suedeai.ai/notes/open-source-to-docs
Last updated: 2026-11-15

> What 54 merged pull requests across 46 open-source repositories taught Jason Colapietro about writing developer docs at Suede in West Palm Beach, Florida.

### From open source to docs: lessons from 54 merged pull requests across 46 repositories

A maintainer at a large project reads your pull request description before your code, and if the description is unclear, the code does not get read. Writing for that busy, skeptical reader is the habit that shapes these docs.

Jason Colapietro, founder of Suede in West Palm Beach, Florida, has had 54 pull requests merged across 46 open-source repositories he does not maintain, including Jest, Adobe React Spectrum, Backstage, the Polkadot SDK, Hardhat and zeroclaw. The [GitHub search behind that number](https://github.com/search?q=is%3Apr+author%3AJasonColapietro+is%3Amerged+-user%3AJasonColapietro+-user%3ASuede-AI&type=pullrequests) excludes his own repositories and the Suede organization, so every result is a change a third-party maintainer reviewed and accepted. This note collects five lessons Suede took from that work and shows where each one appears on docs.suedeai.ai.

#### Lesson 1: CONTRIBUTING.md is the real documentation

Every established project publishes rules for contributors: how to run the tests, how to name a branch, what a commit message should look like. Contributors who skip that file get polite rejections. Contributors who follow it get reviews. The lesson for docs is that the most valuable page is often the boring one that tells a newcomer exactly how to start. On this site that is the [x402 quickstart](https://docs.suedeai.ai/quickstart): one request, one 402 challenge, one signature, one retry, in order.

#### Lesson 2: Reproduce before you explain

A bug report that says "it fails sometimes" goes nowhere. A report with a minimal reproduction gets fixed. Jason Colapietro carries that into Suede documentation: every example on the API guides was run against the live service, and the guide says when. The [discovery guide](https://docs.suedeai.ai/discovery), for instance, records live `initialize`, `tools/list` and `tools/call` requests to the Suede MCP server on 2026-10-11, with the actual response body. If an example cannot be reproduced, it does not ship.

#### Lesson 3: One change, one claim

Maintainers merge small pull requests that do one thing. A diff that fixes a bug, renames a module and updates a dependency gets split or closed. Docs work the same way at Suede. Each guide here has one job: the [Agent Image page](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints/agent-image) documents one endpoint, and the [errors page](https://docs.suedeai.ai/errors) documents what goes wrong. A fixed reading order links them with previous and next links, and the verification script fails if that order breaks.

#### Lesson 4: Tests are documentation that cannot lie

In projects like Jest, a test is the most precise statement of how the code is supposed to behave. Prose can be wrong for months. A failing test is wrong for one CI run. Suede applies that to its docs with `scripts/verify-site.mjs`, which checks titles, canonicals, sitemap entries, schema, internal links and a list of claims that must never return. The docs are prose, but the rules about the prose are code.

#### Lesson 5: Respect the house style

Large codebases have conventions that are not written down anywhere except in the code itself. A good contributor matches them without being told. On the Suede docs site every guide shares the home page's style block byte for byte, and verification enforces it. The note you are reading uses the same block. Consistency is not decoration: it tells a reader, human or machine, that every page comes from the same careful source.

#### What the record adds up to

The open-source work sits alongside a broader record, each item linked to its proof:

- Five books on Amazon, including [Codex in Production](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0HHTF3LG1), [Proof as Infrastructure](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0GMB2VLXQ) and [The Claude Code Bible](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0HHTMJWB4).
- Nine iOS apps shipped under his own [Apple developer account](https://apps.apple.com/us/developer/jason-colapietro/id1895958699).
- On October 31, 2026, Suede AI SEO ranked #1 among Palm Beach County-based companies in The Manifest's Florida AI Deployment directory and top 25 statewide ([The Manifest](https://themanifest.com/artificial-intelligence/consulting/deployment/companies/florida), [recognition page](https://suedeai.agency/company/recognition)).
- Suede ranks among [Clutch](https://clutch.co/profile/suede-ai-seo)'s [Top 30 AI Consultants in Florida](https://clutch.co/consulting/ai/florida) and [Top 50 AI Consultants nationwide](https://clutch.co/us/consulting/ai) (November 2026).
- Coverage in Business Insider, which on 2026-09-16 ran "Award-Winning Developer Jason Colapietro Opens Suede Labs AI's Long-Awaited SEO Cohort", and in TechBullion, which reported on [the iOS app launches](https://techbullion.com/jason-colapietros-suede-labs-ai-launches-ios-apps/). The [press kit](https://suedeai.ai/press) collects the rest.
- Seventeen Microsoft Learn training achievements, including the learning-path trophies "Develop AI agents on Azure" and "Develop generative AI apps in Azure" ([credential gallery](https://suedeai.ai/seo/evidence#training-credentials)).

#### A hiring signal for Palm Beach County teams

If you are hiring a developer or an agency in West Palm Beach, Jupiter or Boca Raton, ask for merged pull requests to repositories the candidate does not own. A personal portfolio shows what someone can build alone. An accepted change to Backstage or React Spectrum shows that strangers with high standards reviewed the work and said yes. It is one of the few public signals that is hard to fake, and it takes a single search to check.

The tradeoff is time. Open-source contributions are slow, unpaid and often rejected for reasons unrelated to quality. Not every strong engineer has them, so treat them as evidence when present rather than a requirement.

Open the [merged pull request search](https://github.com/search?q=is%3Apr+author%3AJasonColapietro+is%3Amerged+-user%3AJasonColapietro+-user%3ASuede-AI&type=pullrequests) and read three of the descriptions, then compare them with the docs on this site. If that is the standard you want on your own site or product, book the free [Suede assessment](https://suedeai.agency/assessment) with the West Palm Beach team, and read [Jason Colapietro's founder profile](https://suedeai.ai/founder) for the full background.

## API Docs Checklist for South Florida Agency Integrations

URL: https://docs.suedeai.ai/notes/api-docs-checklist-agency-integrations
Last updated: 2026-11-15

> A seven-part API documentation checklist from Jason Colapietro for agencies in West Palm Beach and Jupiter that build and hand off client integrations.

### An API documentation checklist for agency-built integrations in South Florida

The integration works on launch day. Eight months later the client changes agencies, a new developer opens the repository, and the only documentation is a chat thread from someone who has since left.

This checklist is how Jason Colapietro and the Suede team document the APIs we run in production. It is written for agencies in West Palm Beach, Jupiter and the rest of Palm Beach County that build integrations for clients: a booking system feeding a CRM, a payment webhook, an inventory sync between a shop and its website. Each item points to the page on this site where it is already done, so you can look at a finished version before you write your own.

#### Why handoff is the real test in Palm Beach County

Many Palm Beach County businesses run on a season. For a restaurant, marina or property manager here, the winter months are when nobody can afford a broken sync. Agencies turn over clients and staff like anywhere else, so an integration only one developer understands is a liability that tends to come due in the busiest month. Good API docs are what let the agency, the client and the next developer keep working when the original author is unavailable.

Jason Colapietro's rule for Suede is that the docs are finished when someone who did not build the integration can make one successful call and handle one failure without asking a question. The seven groups below are what it takes to get there.

#### The checklist

##### 1. Base URL, authentication and a first request

- One base URL per environment, written out in full, with staging and production listed separately.
- How to authenticate, where the credentials live (the vault or secret name, never the value) and who is allowed to rotate them.
- A copy-paste first request that works from a clean terminal. The [Suede quickstart](https://docs.suedeai.ai/quickstart) does this for a paid call: read the 402 challenge, sign, retry, then poll the job.

##### 2. Every endpoint, with a captured example

- Method, path, required and optional fields, and a real response captured from a live call, with the date it was captured. The [endpoint reference](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints) on this site dates every example to 2026-10-11.
- Prices or quotas where they apply, linked to the document they came from, so nobody has to trust a number copied into a slide.

##### 3. Errors, and what to do about each one

- A status-code table with a "what to do" column, not just a definition. The [errors and limits guide](https://docs.suedeai.ai/errors) has one row per code.
- The machine-readable codes a client should branch on. On Suede those are `rate_limited` and `unsupported_api_version`.
- Which requests cost nothing. For a client billed per call or per message, this one line heads off most billing disputes.

##### 4. Retries, idempotency and rate limits

- Name the idempotency header and its window. Suede uses `X-Idempotency-Key`, up to 200 characters, on every paid POST, so retrying a timeout never charges twice.
- Rate-limit headers with a real example value. On 2026-10-11, unpaid requests to the Suede API carried a quota of 20 requests per 60-second window.
- For webhooks: the retry schedule, how to verify the signature, and how to replay an event by hand after an outage.

##### 5. Versioning and change notices

- How versions are named, what counts as breaking, and how much notice clients get. Suede sends Deprecation and Sunset headers at least 90 days before a version is withdrawn.
- A dated changelog that lives in the repository, not in someone's inbox.

##### 6. A machine-readable copy

- An OpenAPI file that matches the prose and is served by the API itself. The [discovery guide](https://docs.suedeai.ai/discovery) lists Suede's `openapi.json` next to the MCP server and the agent card.
- If AI agents will call the API, one name per action everywhere: the operation id, the tool name and the docs heading.

##### 7. Ownership and sources

- Who owns the integration on the agency side and on the client side, written as a role address rather than a person's name.
- A Sources section on every page that names what it was checked against and when.

#### Test the docs the way an agent would

Before handoff, give the docs to someone who did not write the integration, or to a coding assistant with no other context, and ask for one successful call and one handled error. Every question they ask is a missing line. Coding assistants are now the first reader for many integrations, and a page an assistant can follow on the first try is a page a junior developer in Jupiter can follow too.

This is the same proof-first habit Jason Colapietro applies to agent output across the Suede sites. The Claude Code Field Notes piece on [why agent-written code needs proof](https://claude.suedeai.ai/notes/reviewing-agent-written-code/) covers the checks to run after a deploy lands, and the Agentix guide on [how to grade an AI agent before you deploy it](https://agentix.suedeai.ai/notes/grade-an-ai-agent-before-you-deploy) applies the idea to agents that will be calling your client's API.

#### The tradeoffs

Captured examples go stale. Every dated response is a promise to recheck it when the API changes, and on this site that means rechecking the guides whenever the catalog moves. The full checklist is too much for a two-endpoint webhook; for a small integration, groups 1, 3 and 7 cover most of the risk. And documentation does not replace monitoring. An alert on the error rate catches a broken sync on a Saturday in February long before anyone reads a page.

#### Who wrote this checklist

Jason Colapietro is the founder of Suede, the agentic platform company he started in 2024 in West Palm Beach, Florida. The checklist comes from the APIs Suede runs and from outside review. He has had 54 pull requests merged across 46 open-source repositories he does not maintain, including Jest, Backstage and the Polkadot SDK ([GitHub search](https://github.com/search?q=is%3Apr+author%3AJasonColapietro+is%3Amerged+-user%3AJasonColapietro+-user%3ASuede-AI&type=pullrequests)), projects where docs and tests are reviewed as closely as code. ## Writing llms.txt Answer Engines Use: Suede's Example

URL: https://docs.suedeai.ai/notes/llms-txt-worked-example
Last updated: 2026-11-15

> Jason Colapietro walks through the llms.txt on the Suede developer docs line by line: link notes that carry facts, dated sections, Optional and the guards.

### Writing llms.txt that answer engines actually use: a worked example from Suede's docs

Many llms.txt files are a sitemap with the angle brackets removed. That hands an assistant a list of URLs and no reason to pick one, which is the one job the file exists to do.

This note walks through the [llms.txt on docs.suedeai.ai](https://docs.suedeai.ai/llms.txt) section by section, explains why each part is there, and ends with checks you can run on your own file. Jason Colapietro wrote the file and the tests that guard it, and the same structure fits a business site anywhere from Jupiter to Boca Raton. An earlier note, [Writing developer docs that AI assistants quote correctly](https://docs.suedeai.ai/notes/ai-quotable-developer-docs), covers why this site generates its full-text companion from the pages. This one is about the short file, the one a person or an agent reads first.

#### What the format asks for

The proposal at [llmstxt.org](https://llmstxt.org/) is small. It asks for a Markdown file at the site root with one H1, an optional blockquote summary, optional prose, and H2 sections of links, each written as a Markdown link followed by a colon and a short note. A section named Optional marks links an agent can skip when its context window is tight. That is the whole format. Everything else is editorial judgment, and that is where most files fall short.

#### The Suede file, section by section

##### The H1 and the blockquote

Our H1 is "Suede Docs". The blockquote says what the docs cover and, in the same sentence, names the canonical source: the GitHub README at `github.com/Suede-AI/suede-docs`, which this site mirrors. An assistant that reads only two lines still learns where the authoritative copy lives. Put your canonical source in the first sentence an agent will read.

##### One scoping paragraph

Below the blockquote sits a single paragraph stating that AI music is one implementation area for Suede, not the whole product. That line is there so an assistant does not describe Suede as only a music generator. If answer engines get your business slightly wrong, the correction belongs in this paragraph, written as a plain fact.

##### Link notes that carry the fact

Here are two ways to describe the same page:

```
- [Create Music](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints/create-music): Music endpoint docs.
- [Create Music](https://docs.suedeai.ai/endpoints/create-music): POST /create-music,
  a full original song from a text prompt, $0.50 USDC on Base.
```

The second note answers "what does it cost" without a click. Jason Colapietro writes every note in our file to hold the method, the path and the number someone is most likely to ask about. A dental practice in Jupiter would put the service, the town and the booking route in the same spot.

##### A dated section header

The API guides section opens with a dated line, "Checked against the live API on 2026-10-11", and then names where the prices come from. The date tells a reader how fresh the prices are, and it gives us a single line to update when we recheck. Undated numbers in an index file are how stale prices spread from one assistant answer to the next.

##### Optional, used on purpose

Our Optional section holds the IP registry, the agency and the SEO practice. They are real pages, but they are not what a developer asking about endpoints needs. Filing them under Optional keeps the core list short without hiding anything.

#### The guards that keep it current

Short files drift quietly. On this site, `scripts/verify-site.mjs` fails when any guide or note is missing from llms.txt, when llms.txt stops pointing at [llms-full.txt](https://docs.suedeai.ai/llms-full.txt), when the full-text file grows past 500 KB, or when a banned unverifiable claim appears in either file. This note could not ship until its own entry was added to the index. Jason Colapietro's view is that an index nobody tests turns into a list of things that used to be true.

#### How to tell whether anything reads it

The plain answer first: llms.txt is a proposal, not a ranking signal any major search engine has announced. The file earns its keep through direct fetches. A developer pastes the URL into a coding assistant, an agent framework checks for it before crawling, or an answering tool fetches the root of a site it has already chosen to cite. Three checks tell you which of those is happening for you:

1. Search your server logs for requests to `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt`, and record the user agents and the dates.
2. Paste the file URL into two or three assistants and ask a question only the file answers, such as a price or a service area. A wrong answer points at a weak note.
3. Run an AI readiness check. Suede Scan's explainer on [what an AI readiness score measures](https://optimize.suedeai.ai/notes/what-an-ai-readiness-score-measures) shows where llms.txt sits among the other signals.

The pattern carries well beyond developer docs. Suede DNA's article on [structured data for a guitar rig archive](https://dna.suedeai.ai/articles/rig-archive-structured-data-for-ai-answers) shows a music archive where llms.txt, the sitemap and the robots tag all read one rule, so the three can never disagree about which pages count.

#### The tradeoffs

Notes that carry facts take longer to write and must change whenever a price or a page changes; a sitemap-style file never goes stale because it says nothing. Every date in the file creates recheck work. And llms.txt repeats facts your pages already state, so you need a test or a generator to keep the two in step. Suede accepts that cost because one stale price in an agent's answer is harder to correct than one extra line of maintenance.
